77911.m: The Jungfrau Railway has run up to the Jungfraujoch since 1912.

77912.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77912.e: In the evening, the street lamps were lit with fire and a ladder. That was the job of the lamplighter, before there was electric light.
77912.m: In the past, lamplighters lit the street lamps every evening.

77913.q: Which job from the past do these pictures mean?
77913.e: Wood, fire and black charcoal show the charcoal burner. He slowly charred wood in a kiln with little air and made charcoal this way.
77913.m: The charcoal burner made charcoal in a kiln.

77914.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77914.e: A basket of clothes by the water shows the washerwoman. Without washing machines, washerwomen washed clothes by hand in a stream or at a fountain.
77914.m: In the past, washerwomen washed the laundry by hand.

77915.q: Which craft is meant by these pictures?
77915.e: A barrel, wood and a hammer show the cooper. He makes barrels from wooden staves and iron hoops.

77916.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77916.e: Letters, horses, the post horn and mountains show the stagecoach driver. Before there was a railway, stagecoaches travelled, for example, over the Gotthard Pass.
77916.m: Stagecoach drivers blew the post horn and carried post and travellers over the passes.

77917.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77917.e: Grain, a mill wheel and water show the miller. In the watermill, he grinds grain into flour.
77917.m: The miller grinds grain into flour.

77918.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77918.e: A horn, the night and a village show the night watchman. He walked through the lanes at night, called out the hours and sounded the alarm if there was a fire.
77918.m: The night watchman called out the hours at night.

77919.q: Which craft is meant by these pictures?
77919.e: Knotted cords and twisting show the rope maker. He twisted fibres from hemp into cords and ropes.
77919.m: The rope maker twists fibres into ropes.

77920.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77920.e: A woman at a computer who fixes errors in the program (“bugs”) is a computer scientist. She develops and repairs software.
77920.m: Computer scientists develop programs for computers.

77921.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77921.e: A building, a set square and a house show the architect. She plans and designs buildings.
77921.m: An architect plans and designs buildings.

77922.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77922.e: Hair, scissors and a mirror show the hairdresser. She cuts, colours and styles hair.
77922.m: A hairdresser cuts and styles hair.

77923.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77923.e: A gateau, a slice of cake and a cupcake show the pastry chef. She bakes and decorates gateaux and fine cakes.
77923.m: A pastry chef makes gateaux and cakes.

77924.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77924.e: A test tube, a microscope and a lab coat show the lab technician. She carries out experiments and measurements in the laboratory.
77924.m: Lab technicians work with microscopes and test tubes.

77925.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77925.e: Medicines, a prescription and a shop show the pharmacist. She hands out medicines and gives advice on how to take them.
77925.m: In the chemist's, pharmacists give advice about medicines.

77926.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77926.e: Trees, a saw and a worker with a helmet show the forester. He looks after the forest and cuts down trees.
77926.m: A forester looks after the forest.

77927.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77927.e: A newspaper, a microphone and a camera show the journalist. She researches and reports on news.
77927.m: Journalists research and report on news.

77928.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77928.e: Volleyball and beach make beach volleyball. It is played in pairs on sand.
77928.m: In beach volleyball, two play against two on sand.

77929.q: Which team sport do these pictures show?
77929.e: Water, swimming and a ball stand for water polo. Two teams swim and throw a ball into the other team's goal.
77929.m: In water polo, you throw the ball into the goal while swimming.

77930.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77930.e: Running in the forest with a map and compass is orienteering. You try to find checkpoints in the terrain as fast as possible.
77930.m: In orienteering, you find the checkpoints with a map and compass.

77931.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77931.e: A sailing boat, wind and the chequered flag show sailing. The Swiss team Alinghi won the America's Cup in 2003.
77931.m: In sailing, the wind drives the boat.

77932.q: Which Swiss sport do these pictures show?
77932.e: Two fighters in sawdust from wood and a bull as a prize go with Schwingen, Swiss wrestling. The winner at the Federal Wrestling Festival often gets a bull.
77932.m: In Schwingen, two wrestlers fight in a ring of sawdust.

77933.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77933.e: A flag in the hole and a player with a club show golf. The aim is to get the ball into the hole with as few strokes as possible.
77933.m: In golf, you need as few strokes as possible to reach the hole.

77934.q: Which competition do these pictures mean?
77934.e: A rider at a gallop and the chequered flag make a horse race. In St Moritz, horse races even take place on the frozen lake.
77934.m: In a horse race, the fastest horse wins.

77935.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77935.e: Art (paint palette) and gymnastics make artistic gymnastics. You do exercises on apparatus such as the high bar, parallel bars and floor.
77935.m: In artistic gymnastics, you perform on different pieces of apparatus.

77936.q: Which sport do these pictures mean?
77936.e: Mountain and bike make mountain bike. You ride a mountain bike off-road and in the mountains.
77936.m: With a mountain bike you can ride over rough ground.

77937.q: Which Olympic custom do these pictures mean?
77937.e: Fire and a runner make the torch relay. The Olympic flame is lit in Olympia in Greece and carried to the host city.
77937.m: The Olympic flame is lit in Olympia.

77938.q: Which symbol do these pictures mean?
77938.e: Five rings are the symbol of the Olympic Games. They stand for the five continents that come together at the Games.
77938.m: The five Olympic rings stand for the five continents.

77939.q: Which prize for winners at the ancient Olympic Games do these pictures show?
77939.e: A Greek temple, olives and a crown show the olive wreath. In ancient Olympia, the winners received a wreath made from branches of the olive tree.
77939.m: In ancient times, Olympic winners received an olive wreath.

77940.q: Which major event do these pictures mean?
77940.e: Snow, mountains and a medal go with the Winter Olympics. In Switzerland, they took place in St Moritz in 1928 and 1948.
77940.m: St Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

77941.q: What do the best stand on at the award ceremony, as these pictures show?
77941.e: First, second and third places and a gold medal show the winners' podium. The winner stands in the middle on the highest step.
77941.m: On the winners' podium, the winner stands at the top.

77942.q: Which athletics event do these pictures show?
77942.e: A runner and several barriers stand for the hurdles. You have to jump over hurdles while running.
77942.m: In the hurdles, you jump over hurdles at full speed.

77943.q: Which athletics event do these pictures show?
77943.e: A long jump like a kangaroo's and a sandpit make long jump. After the run-up, you land in a pit of sand.
77943.m: In the long jump, you land in the sandpit.

77944.q: Which games do these pictures mean?
77944.e: A wheelchair and a medal in the stadium show the Paralympic Games. Athletes with disabilities compete there.
77944.m: At the Paralympics, people with disabilities compete.

77945.q: Which winter sport do these pictures show?
77945.e: A curling stone, a brush and ice show curling. The players sweep in front of the stone so that it slides further.
77945.m: In curling, you sweep the ice in front of the stone.

77946.q: Which winter sport do these pictures show?
77946.e: Sticks with a puck, ice and a goal show ice hockey. Each team has five outfield players and a goalkeeper on the ice.
77946.m: In ice hockey, you shoot the puck into the goal.

77947.q: Which winter sport do these pictures show?
77947.e: A sledge, the number four, ice and the chequered flag make the four-man bobsleigh. In St Moritz there is a bobsleigh run made of natural ice.
77947.m: Four people sit in a four-man bobsleigh.

77948.q: Which winter sport do these pictures mean?
77948.e: Snow and surfing make snowboarding, because you stand sideways on a board. Snowboarding has been an Olympic sport since 1998.
77948.m: In snowboarding, you stand sideways on a board.

77950.q: Which skiing event do these pictures show?
77950.e: A skier between lots of flags shows the slalom. You ski tightly around lots of gates.
77950.m: In the slalom, you ski around lots of tight gates.

77951.q: Which winter sport do these pictures mean?
77951.e: Dogs, a sledge and snow show sled dog racing. Huskies often pull the sledge.
77951.m: In sled dog racing, dogs pull the sledge.

77952.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77952.e: Ice, speed (lightning) and running make speed skating. You skate around a 400-metre track.
77952.m: In speed skating, only the time counts.

77953.q: Which instrument do these pictures make together?
77953.e: A mouth and an organ make mouth organ, another name for the harmonica. You blow and suck air through small channels.
77953.m: You play the mouth organ with your mouth.

77954.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77954.e: A church and a keyboard show the church organ. It is played with hands and feet and has lots of pipes.
77954.m: You play the organ with your hands and feet.

77955.q: Which instrument do these pictures make together?
77955.e: Bell (Glocke) and game (Spiel, the dice) make glockenspiel, a German word that is also used in English. You strike small metal bars with little mallets.
77955.m: On a glockenspiel, you strike metal bars.

77956.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77956.e: The stringed instrument with a round drum and the cowboy show the banjo. It is very popular in the folk music of the USA.
77956.m: The banjo has a round body like a drum.

77957.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77957.e: A stringed instrument and a very tall giraffe show the double bass. It is the largest and deepest stringed instrument in the orchestra.
77957.m: The double bass is the largest stringed instrument.

77958.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77958.e: A small guitar, flowers and an island show the ukulele. It comes from Hawaii and has four strings.
77958.m: The ukulele is a small guitar from Hawaii.

77959.q: Which instrument do these pictures make together?
77959.e: Electricity (lightning) and guitar make electric guitar. It needs an amplifier so that you can hear it loudly.
77959.m: The electric guitar needs an amplifier.

77960.q: Which Swiss folk instrument do these pictures show?
77960.e: A small accordion and the mountains show the Schwyzerörgeli. It is often played in Swiss folk music.
77960.m: The Schwyzerörgeli is a small accordion from Switzerland.

77961.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77961.e: A kangaroo for Australia, wood and music show the didgeridoo. It is a long wind instrument of the Aborigines made from a hollow branch.

77962.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77962.e: A saxophone, a piano and a club at night go with jazz. Jazz began around 1900 in New Orleans and is all about improvising.

77963.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77963.e: A microphone, a cap and a speaking head show rap. In rap, you speak words rhythmically to the music.
77963.m: In rap, you speak words to a rhythm.

77964.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77964.e: A cowboy hat, a guitar and a horse go with country music. It comes from rural areas of the USA.
77964.m: Country music comes from the USA.

77965.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77965.e: A violin, a piano and an old clock go with classical music. Well-known composers are Mozart and Beethoven.
77965.m: Mozart and Beethoven wrote classical music.

77966.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77966.e: An island, music and the colours green, yellow and red show reggae. Reggae comes from Jamaica and became famous through Bob Marley.

77967.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77967.e: Blue, a guitar and a sad face show the blues. “To have the blues” means to be sad.

77968.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77968.e: A church, raised hands and music show gospel. Gospel songs are Christian songs from African American churches.
77968.m: Gospel is often sung by large choirs.

77969.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77969.e: Heavy, metal and a guitar make heavy metal. Loud, distorted guitars are typical.
77969.m: Heavy metal is loud rock music with distorted guitars.

77970.q: Which famous ballet do these pictures show?
77970.e: Ballet shoes, a swan and water show “Swan Lake”. The music was written by Pyotr Tchaikovsky.
77970.m: The music for “Swan Lake” is by Tchaikovsky.

77971.q: Which Christmas ballet do these pictures show?
77971.e: A nut being cracked, ballet shoes and a Christmas tree show “The Nutcracker”. Tchaikovsky's ballet takes place on Christmas Eve.

77972.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77972.e: Carnival, drums, dancing and a beach go with the samba. It comes from Brazil and is danced at the carnival in Rio.

77973.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77973.e: Loud shoes to music show tap dance. The shoes have metal plates that click when you dance.
77973.m: In tap dance, metal plates on the shoes click.

77974.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77974.e: The number three, a dancing couple and violins show the waltz. It is danced in three-four time, especially in Vienna.
77974.m: The waltz is danced in three-four time.

77975.q: Which Italian folk dance do these pictures mean?
77975.e: A spider (tarantula) and dancing show the tarantella. According to an old legend, fast dancing was supposed to help against a tarantula bite.
77975.m: The tarantella is a fast dance from southern Italy.

77976.q: Which Spanish dance do these pictures mean?
77976.e: A ruffled dress, clapping, a guitar and a rose show flamenco. It comes from Andalusia in Spain.

77977.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77977.e: Acrobatics, spins, a cap and music show breakdance. It is part of hip-hop culture from New York.
77977.m: Breakdance is part of hip-hop culture.

77979.q: Which dice game do these pictures show?
77979.e: Snakes, ladders and a dice show snakes and ladders. You climb up the ladders and slide down the snakes.
77979.m: In snakes and ladders, you slide down the snakes.

77980.q: Which board game do these pictures mean?
77980.e: A pawn, a king and a horse show chess. The horse is called the knight, and you want to checkmate the king.
77980.m: In chess, you want to checkmate the king.

77983.q: Which Swiss card game do these pictures mean?
77983.e: Playing cards with roses, acorns, bells and shields show Jass. It is the best-known card game in Switzerland.
77983.m: Jass is the most popular card game in Switzerland.

77984.q: Which puzzle game do these pictures mean?
77984.e: A puzzle piece and a picture show the jigsaw puzzle. You put lots of small pieces together to make a whole picture.
77984.m: In a jigsaw puzzle, you put pieces together to make a picture.

77986.q: Which device do these pictures make together?
77986.e: Needle, thread and a machine make sewing machine. With it, you sew fabric much faster than by hand.
77986.m: With a sewing machine you sew faster than by hand.

77987.q: Which hobby do these pictures show?
77987.e: A fishing rod, a fish and a river show fishing. In Switzerland you usually need a licence for it.
77987.m: In Switzerland you usually need a licence to go fishing.

77988.q: Which hobby do these pictures show?
77988.e: A seedling, a potted plant and water show gardening. Plants need soil, light and water.
77988.m: In gardening, you look after plants.

77989.q: What are you building, as these pictures show?
77989.e: A bird, a house and a hammer make the birdhouse. In winter you can feed birds in it.
77989.m: You build a birdhouse for birds.

77990.q: Which hobby do these pictures show?
77990.e: Scissors, paper and coloured pencils show crafts. You cut, stick and paint.
77990.m: In crafts, you cut and stick.

77991.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77991.e: Climbing and wall make climbing wall. In climbing centres there are walls with colourful holds.
77991.m: On a climbing wall, you hold on to holds.

77992.q: Which leisure activity do these pictures show?
77992.e: A kite and wind show kite flying. In autumn it is often windy enough for it.
77992.m: You need wind to fly a kite.

77994.q: Which paper craft do these pictures mean?
77994.e: Paper, a bird and Japan show origami. In this Japanese art, you fold figures such as the crane out of paper.
77994.m: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

77995.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77995.e: Air (aeroplane) and port (anchor) make airport. The largest airport in Switzerland is in Zurich.
77995.m: The largest airport in Switzerland is near Zurich.

77996.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77996.e: Train and ticket make train ticket. In Switzerland, people say “Billett” for a ticket.
77996.m: You need a ticket to travel by train.

77997.q: Which travel document do these pictures mean?
77997.e: Passport control, a red booklet and a suitcase show the passport. The Swiss passport is red.

77998.q: Which book do these pictures mean?
77998.e: Travel, a book and good tips make a travel guide. It describes the sights at a holiday destination.
77998.m: A travel guide gives tips for your destination.

77999.q: Which famous Swiss train do these pictures mean?
77999.e: A glacier, a train and mountains show the Glacier Express. It runs from Zermatt to St Moritz and is said to be the slowest express train in the world.
77999.m: The Glacier Express runs from Zermatt to St Moritz.

78000.q: What kind of journey do these pictures show?
78000.e: A big ship, the sea and islands show a cruise. You travel on a ship and visit several places.
78000.m: On a cruise, you live on a ship.

78001.q: Which travel problem do these pictures mean?
78001.e: Flying, a different time and tiredness show jet lag. It happens when you fly quickly across several time zones.
78001.m: Jet lag comes from flights across time zones.

78002.q: Which means of transport do these pictures make together?
78002.e: Cable, car and mountain make cable car. The cabin hangs from cables and travels up the mountain.
78002.m: On a cable car, the cabin hangs from cables.

78003.q: Which holiday activity do these pictures show?
78003.e: Hiking boots, a mountain and a map show hiking. Switzerland has a dense network of footpaths marked in yellow.
78003.m: Swiss footpaths are marked in yellow.

78004.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78004.e: Air and bed (mattress) make airbed. You can lie on it by the water or sleep on it in a tent.
78004.m: An airbed is filled with air.

78005.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78005.e: Sun and umbrella make sun umbrella. It gives shade on the beach or in the garden.

78006.q: What kind of holiday do these pictures show?
78006.e: A tent, a campfire and a forest show a camp. The Scouts, for example, often go to camp in summer.
78006.m: At camp, you sleep in a tent.

78008.q: Which feeling on holiday do these pictures mean?
78008.e: A house, a thought and sadness show homesickness. You miss your home, for example at camp.
78008.m: Homesickness means you miss your home.

78009.e: A postbox, a picture and the beach show the picture postcard. It shows a picture of the holiday place and is sent by post.
78009.m: People like to send a postcard from their holidays.

78010.q: Which holiday problem do these pictures mean?
78010.e: Lots of cars and a snail show the traffic jam. At the start of the holidays, there are often traffic jams in front of the Gotthard road tunnel.
78010.m: At the start of the holidays, there are often traffic jams at the Gotthard.

78011.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78011.e: A pumpkin, sweets and a ghost show Halloween. It is celebrated on 31 October.

78012.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78012.e: Masks, drums, trumpets and confetti show carnival (Fasnacht). The Basel carnival has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage since 2017.

78013.q: Which public holiday do these pictures mean?
78013.e: The numbers 1 and 8, fireworks and paper lanterns show Swiss National Day on 1 August. It is the national holiday of Switzerland.
78013.m: Switzerland's national holiday is on 1 August.

78014.q: Which Zurich festival do these pictures mean?
78014.e: A snowman in the fire, horses and six o'clock show Sechseläuten. At 6 p.m., the Böögg is set alight, and riders circle the fire.
78014.m: At Sechseläuten, the Böögg is burnt.

78015.q: Which market in Bern do these pictures mean?
78015.e: Onions, shopping and the bear for Bern show the Zibelemärit, the onion market. It takes place every year on the fourth Monday in November.
78015.m: The Zibelemärit is an onion market in Bern.

78016.q: Which Swiss custom do these pictures mean?
78016.e: Decorated cows with bells coming down the mountain show the Alpine descent. In autumn, the animals come back from the Alpine pastures to the valley.
78016.m: In the Alpine descent, the cows return to the valley in autumn.

78017.q: Who comes on 6 December with these pictures?
78017.e: A man with a beard, mandarins and nuts show the Samichlaus, the Swiss St Nicholas. He comes on 6 December, often together with Schmutzli.

78018.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78018.e: A big wheel, a merry-go-round and sweets show the Chilbi. That is what a funfair is called in Switzerland.
78018.m: A Chilbi is a funfair with rides.

78019.q: Which time of the church year do these pictures mean?
78019.e: Fir branches, candles and the number four show Advent. The Advent wreath has four candles for the four Sundays before Christmas.
78019.m: Four candles burn on the Advent wreath.

78021.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78021.e: Hearing (ear) and book make audiobook. A book is read aloud and you listen.
78021.m: You listen to an audiobook instead of reading it.

78022.q: Which place do these pictures mean?
78022.e: A clapperboard, popcorn and a ticket show the cinema. There you watch films on a big screen.
78022.m: At the cinema, you watch films on a screen.

78023.q: What kind of photo do these pictures mean?
78023.e: If you point your mobile at yourself, you take a selfie. A selfie is a photo you take of yourself.
78023.m: A selfie is a photo of yourself.

78024.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78024.e: Computer and game (controller) make computer game. With games, you should pay attention to the recommended age.
78024.m: With computer games, you check the age rating.

78025.q: What kind of film do these pictures mean?
78025.e: A pencil, a film strip and a mouse show the cartoon. Lots of drawn pictures are shown quickly one after another.
78025.m: A cartoon is made of lots of drawn pictures.

78026.q: What kind of film do these pictures mean?
78026.e: No sound, a film strip and a hat like Charlie Chaplin's show the silent film. Until the end of the 1920s, films mostly had no spoken sound.
78026.m: Silent films have no spoken sound.

78027.q: Which programme do these pictures mean?
78027.e: Sun and clouds, a television and a map show the weather forecast. It predicts the weather for the next few days.
78027.m: The weather forecast predicts the weather.

78098.q: Which saying with a colour does this picture puzzle show?
78098.e: Among several sheep, a black one stands out. “The black sheep” is someone who stands out in a group in a bad way.
78098.m: The black sheep of a family stands out because of bad behaviour.

78204.q: Which Bible story do these emojis show?
78204.e: A big ship, animals in pairs, rain, a dove and a rainbow: Noah saves his family and the animals from the Flood.
78204.m: After the Flood, Noah sent out a dove, which came back with an olive branch.

78346.q: Which animal behaviour do these pictures mean?
78346.e: In autumn, birds fly to warmer parts of the world. This behaviour is called bird migration; swallows from Switzerland, for example, spend the winter in Africa.
78346.m: Migratory birds spend the winter in warmer regions.

78393.e: A dinosaur in rock stands for a fossil. Fossils are the remains or traces of living things from earlier ages of the Earth, turned to stone.
78393.m: Fossils are evidence of life from prehistoric times.

78405.q: Which form of energy do these pictures mean?
78405.e: Wind turns a wheel, and this makes electricity. Wind turbines turn the movement energy of the air into electrical energy.
78405.m: Wind turbines use the movement energy of the air.

78428.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78428.e: The maple leaf is on Canada's flag, the beaver is an official national symbol and ice hockey is the national winter sport. Together, that makes Canada.
78428.m: Canada is the second largest country on Earth by area.

78429.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78429.e: Koalas live in the wild only in Australia, and almost all kangaroos live there too. The dry outback covers large parts of the country.
78429.m: Australia is both a country and a whole continent.

78430.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78430.e: Tacos, cacti and the colourful piñata are seen as typical of Mexico. Maize for tortillas was grown there thousands of years ago.
78430.m: Mexico is the Spanish-speaking country with the most people in the world.

78431.e: The picture shows Mount Fuji, the highest mountain in Japan, along with sushi and the Shinkansen high-speed train, which has been running since 1964.
78431.m: Mount Fuji is a volcano and, at 3776 metres, the highest mountain in Japan.

78432.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78432.e: The giant panda lives in the wild only in China; chopsticks and red lanterns, for example at the Lantern Festival, are part of Chinese culture.
78432.m: China is one of the countries with the most people on Earth.

78433.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78433.e: Elephants, curries and yoga, which has its origins in India, together point to India.

78434.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78434.e: Camels in the desert, the pyramids and the crocodiles in the Nile point to Egypt.
78434.m: Egypt lies in north-east Africa on the Nile.

78437.q: Which city do these emojis mean?
78437.e: The bear is on the coat of arms of Bern, the Federal Palace is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament, and in clear weather you can see the Alps. Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.
78437.m: Officially, Switzerland has no capital; Bern is the federal city.

78438.q: Which capital do these pictures show?
78438.e: The gate stands for the Brandenburg Gate, the bear for the city's coat of arms and the wall for the Berlin Wall, which divided the city from 1961 to 1989.
78438.m: The Wall divided Berlin into East and West for 28 years.

78440.q: Which capital do these emojis show?
78440.e: The stadium stands for the Colosseum, the fountain for the Trevi Fountain, pasta and scooters for Italian city life. Together that makes the Italian capital.
78440.m: The Colosseum is the largest amphitheatre of the ancient world.

78441.e: The guards outside Buckingham Palace, the red double-decker buses and the frequent rain are seen as typical of London.
78441.m: London lies on the Thames and is the capital of the United Kingdom.

78445.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
78445.e: The statue holds a torch and a tablet with the date of the Declaration of Independence. France gave it to the USA, and it was unveiled in New York in 1886.
78445.m: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the USA.

78471.q: Which form of trade do these emojis show?
78471.e: The arrows in a circle show that a cow is swapped directly for grain, without any money at all.
78471.m: In barter, goods are swapped for each other without money.

78473.e: The goods leave your own country and go out into the world. Selling goods abroad is called exporting.
78473.m: Exports are goods that are sold abroad.

78511.e: The ticket divided by two makes half the price. With the Half Fare Travelcard, you travel on Swiss public transport at half price.
78511.m: With the Half Fare Travelcard, you pay only half price on public transport.

78515.e: Red plus sea makes the Red Sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, which is known for its colourful coral reefs and fish.
78515.m: The Red Sea is famous for its coral reefs.

78517.q: Which sea do these emojis show?
78517.e: Olives, lemons and lots of sun typically grow and thrive around the Mediterranean Sea, which separates Europe, Africa and Asia.
78517.m: Around the Mediterranean, there is a warm climate with dry summers.

78519.q: Which natural phenomenon do these emojis show?
78519.e: The pull of the Moon makes the sea level rise and fall regularly. This change between low tide and high tide is called the tides.
78519.m: Low and high tide are caused mainly by the pull of the Moon.

78520.q: Which climate zone do these emojis show?
78520.e: Palm trees, lots of rain and high temperatures all year round mark the tropics around the equator.
78520.m: In the tropics it is warm all year round.

78521.e: Penguins, snow and the polar night lasting for months mark the coldest areas of the Earth at the poles.
78521.m: In the polar zone, there is the polar night in winter.

78525.q: Which climate zone do these pictures mean?
78525.e: Autumn, spring, summer and winter show the four clear seasons. They mark the temperate zone, where Switzerland lies too.
78525.m: Switzerland lies in the temperate climate zone.

78527.q: Which vegetation zone do these emojis show?
78527.e: Sand, dromedaries, cacti and strong sun mark the desert. So little rain falls there that hardly any plants grow.
78527.m: Very little rain falls in the desert.

78573.q: Which technology do these emojis show?
78573.e: The computer receives a radio signal and needs no network cable. A wireless local network is called Wi-Fi or WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network).
78573.m: Wi-Fi connects devices to the network without cables.

78585.q: Which kind of picture do these emojis show?
78585.e: A painter looks in the mirror and paints himself. A picture like this is called a self-portrait; those by Rembrandt, for example, are famous.
78585.m: In a self-portrait, artists show themselves.

78588.q: Which art technique do these emojis mean?
78588.e: Lots of small coloured squares together make a picture. In a mosaic, you put small stones or pieces of glass together to make a picture.
78588.m: A mosaic is made of lots of small coloured stones.

78589.q: Which painting technique goes with these emojis?
78589.e: Painting is done on paper with water, a brush and paint. Painting with see-through water-based paints is called watercolour (in German “Aquarell”, from Latin aqua, water).
78589.m: A watercolour is painted with water-based paints.

78606.q: Which running event do these pictures mean?
78606.e: The number 42 stands for the distance of 42.195 kilometres. This long-distance race is called a marathon, named after the Greek town of Marathon.

78607.q: Which sport do these emojis show?
78607.e: Swimming, cycling and running are done straight after each other. This endurance sport is called triathlon (Greek tri, three).
78607.m: The triathlon is made up of swimming, cycling and running.

78609.e: A ball lies about 11 metres in front of the goal, and only the goalkeeper may try to stop it. This kick is called a penalty.
78609.m: A penalty is taken from the penalty spot.

78622.q: Which job with a French name goes with these emojis?
78622.e: A person with a cap drives other people in a car. Someone who drives a vehicle as a job is called a chauffeur.
78622.m: A chauffeur drives other people in a car.

78623.q: Which job with a French name is meant?
78623.e: Hair is cut with scissors, and the striped sign stands for a salon. In Switzerland, a hairdresser is called a coiffeur.
78623.m: The coiffeur cuts and styles hair.

78631.q: Which painting do these emojis mean?
78631.e: Leonardo da Vinci painted the woman with the mysterious smile in front of a wide landscape; the picture hangs today in the Louvre in Paris.
78631.m: The Mona Lisa's smile is seen as the most famous in the history of art.

78764.q: Which term from psychology do these pictures mean?
78764.e: Sun and a thought bubble with a sleepy face make day and dream. In a daydream, your thoughts wander while you are awake.
78764.m: In a daydream, your thoughts wander even though you are awake.

78778.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures mean?
78778.e: A screen (mobile and computer) is photographed. A photo of the screen is called a screenshot.
78778.m: With a screenshot, you save a picture of the screen.

78790.q: Which term from linguistics do these pictures mean?
78790.e: Hands and hand signs replace the spoken word. Deaf people communicate with sign language; in Switzerland there are three sign languages.
78790.m: Sign languages are full languages that work with the hands, the face and the body.

79416.q: What does baking powder do in cake mixture?
a: It makes the mixture rock hard
79416.e: Baking powder forms lots of tiny gas bubbles in the mixture. These make the cake light and tall.
79416.m: Baking powder makes the mixture rise.

79417.q: Which gas is produced when baking powder works in dough?
79417.e: Baking powder releases the gas carbon dioxide. The gas bubbles puff up the dough.
79417.m: Baking powder makes the gas carbon dioxide.

79418.q: What is a sponge cake like if you forget the baking powder?
79418.e: Without baking powder, hardly any gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake does not rise and stays flat and dense.
79418.m: Without baking powder, the cake stays flat.

79419.q: Where does baking powder work best?
79419.e: Baking powder needs moisture and, above all, heat. In a hot oven it makes the most gas.
79419.m: Baking powder works mainly in a hot oven.

79420.e: Baking powder is a fine white powder. That is why you can hardly see it in the mixture.
79420.m: Baking powder is a white powder.

79421.q: Which substance is the most important part of baking powder?
79421.e: Bicarbonate of soda forms gas bubbles in moist, warm dough. That is why it is the most important part of baking powder.
79421.m: Baking powder is mainly bicarbonate of soda.

79422.q: Why does a cake made with baking powder have lots of little holes inside?
79422.e: During baking, lots of gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake sets and the holes stay.
79422.m: The holes in a cake come from gas bubbles.

79423.q: Which bake is usually made with baking powder?
79423.e: Cakes such as marble cake rise with baking powder. Pizza and bread are usually made with yeast.
79423.m: Marble cake is made with baking powder.

79424.e: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi. You can only see the single yeast cells under a microscope.
79424.m: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi.

79425.q: What do the yeast fungi in dough like to eat most?
79425.e: Yeast fungi feed on sugar. As they do, they make gas that puffs up the dough.

79426.q: What makes a yeast dough rise?
79426.e: The yeast fungi make lots of gas bubbles in the dough. This gas makes the dough big and airy.
79426.m: Yeast makes the dough rise with gas.

79427.q: Where does a yeast dough rise fastest?
79427.e: Yeast likes it warm. In a warm place the yeast fungi work quickly, in the cold only slowly.
79427.m: Yeast dough rises quickly in the warmth.

79428.q: What happens to yeast when it gets very hot?
79428.e: Yeast is made of living things. In great heat they die, for example in the hot oven during baking.

79429.q: Which Swiss Sunday bake is made with yeast?
79429.e: Zopf, a plaited loaf, is made with yeast. The yeast makes it nice and soft and airy.

79430.q: What do you call the process in which yeast makes gas and a little alcohol?
79430.e: This process is called fermentation. The gas makes the dough rise, and the alcohol evaporates during baking.

79431.q: In what form do you often buy fresh yeast in the shop?
79431.e: Fresh yeast is usually sold as a small cube. Dried yeast comes as a powder in a sachet.
79431.m: Fresh yeast is bought as a cube.

79432.e: Vinegar contains an acid. That is why it tastes sour.

79433.q: What is vinegar often used for in the kitchen?
79433.e: Vinegar gives salad dressing a sour taste. It is usually mixed with oil and spices.
79433.m: Vinegar is used for salad dressing.

79434.e: The acetic acid evaporates easily and stings the nose. That is why vinegar smells sharp and sour.

79435.q: What can you remove from a kettle with vinegar?
79435.e: The acid in vinegar dissolves limescale. That is why diluted vinegar helps against white limescale rings.

79436.q: What is cider vinegar made from?
79436.e: Cider vinegar is made from apple juice or cider. This slowly turns sour.
79436.m: Cider vinegar is made from apples.

79437.q: Which tiny living things turn wine into vinegar?
79437.e: Acetic acid bacteria turn the alcohol in wine into acetic acid. This is how wine vinegar is made.

79438.q: Why are gherkins pickled in vinegar?
a: So they go soft like mush
79438.e: The acid in vinegar stops many germs. So pickled gherkins stay good to eat for a long time.

79439.q: What happens to the shell of a raw egg that lies in vinegar for days?
79439.e: The acid in vinegar attacks the hard shell. After a few days only the thin skin is left, and the egg is soft like a rubber ball.

79440.q: What do you often get after eating something very salty?
79440.e: The body has to balance a lot of salt in food with water. That is why you are often very thirsty after salty food.

79441.q: Where does most of the salt in Switzerland come from?
79441.e: Deep underground in Switzerland there are ancient layers of salt. The salt is dissolved out with water, and then the water is evaporated.

79442.q: In which place in the canton of Vaud can you visit an old salt mine?
79442.e: Salt has been mined in Bex for centuries. Visitors can ride into the mine on a little train.
79442.m: There is a salt mine in Bex.

79443.q: Why do you add a pinch of salt to the water for cooking pasta?
79443.e: The pasta takes up a little salt while cooking. That makes it taste more flavourful.
79443.m: Salt in the cooking water gives pasta flavour.

79444.q: What do grains of salt look like under a magnifying glass?
79444.e: Table salt forms cube-shaped crystals. With a magnifying glass you can see the little cubes well.
79444.m: Grains of salt are little cubes.

79445.q: Why is salt spread on icy roads in winter?
79445.e: Salt makes ice melt even in the cold. This makes roads and pavements less slippery.

79446.q: Which substance is added to table salt in Switzerland to keep the thyroid healthy?
79446.e: The body needs iodine for the thyroid gland. That is why Switzerland has had iodised table salt for over 100 years.

79447.q: What do you knead salt dough for crafts from?
79447.e: Salt dough is kneaded from flour, salt and water. After drying or baking it goes hard, and you can paint it.
79447.m: Salt dough is made from flour, salt and water.

79448.q: Which plant is sugar made from in Switzerland?
79448.e: In Switzerland, sugar beet grows in many fields. Sugar is made from its juice.
79448.m: Swiss sugar comes from sugar beet.

79449.q: In which place in the canton of Bern is there a large Swiss sugar factory?
79449.e: Sugar has been made in Aarberg for over 100 years. A second sugar factory is in Frauenfeld.
79449.m: There is a sugar factory in Aarberg.

79450.q: What happens if you stir a lot of sugar into a small glass of water?
79450.e: Water can only dissolve a certain amount of sugar. Anything extra stays at the bottom as grains.
79450.m: Water cannot dissolve endless amounts of sugar.

79451.q: Which plant is much sugar made from in warm countries?
79451.e: Sugar cane is a tall grass that grows in warm countries. Its stalks are full of sweet juice.
79451.m: In warm countries, sugar is made from sugar cane.

79452.q: Which sugar is as fine as flour?
79452.e: Icing sugar is very finely ground sugar. It is used for dusting or for icing.
79452.m: Icing sugar is as fine as flour.

79453.q: What can lots of sweets cause in your teeth?
79453.e: Bacteria in the mouth turn sugar into acid. This acid can attack the teeth and cause tooth decay.
79453.m: Too much sugar can cause tooth decay.

79454.q: What is sugar pressed into little blocks called?
79454.e: Sugar cubes are made of pressed sugar crystals. This makes them easy to count.

79455.e: Green leaves make sugar with sunlight, water and air. The plant stores it, for example, in fruits or roots.
79455.m: Plants make sugar in their green leaves.

79456.q: What do you get when a machine spins melted sugar into fine threads?
79456.e: The machine melts sugar and spins it through tiny holes. The threads set at once and form a cloud.
79456.m: Candyfloss is made of fine sugar threads.

79457.q: What do you sprinkle on crème brûlée before browning it with a flame?
79457.e: Under the hot flame, the sugar melts and turns brown. This makes a crunchy crust on top.
79457.m: Sugar is sprinkled on crème brûlée.

79458.q: What is melted brown sugar called?
79458.e: When sugar is heated strongly, it melts and turns brown. This is called caramel.
79458.m: Brown, melted sugar is called caramel.

79459.q: What does sugar smell like when it caramelises?
79459.e: When sugar caramelises, new scents are formed. That is why it smells sweet and slightly toasted.

79460.q: What happens if you heat caramel for far too long?
79460.e: Sugar heated for too long burns. Then it turns black and tastes bitter.
79460.m: Caramel that gets too hot burns and turns bitter.

79461.q: Why is liquid caramel in the pan dangerous?
a: It is hotter than boiling water
79461.e: Caramel only forms well above 100 degrees. It sticks to the skin and burns it badly.

79462.q: Which Swiss dessert has a caramel sauce?
79462.e: Caramelköpfli is a pudding with a brown caramel sauce. You turn it out onto a plate.

79463.q: What happens to liquid caramel when it cools down?
79463.e: As it cools, liquid caramel sets and becomes as hard as glass. This is how hard sweets are made.

79464.q: Which fairground treat has a coating of caramel?
79464.e: Caramelised almonds are heated with sugar in a pan. The sugar caramelises and coats the almonds.
79464.m: Caramelised almonds have a caramel coating.

79465.q: Which Swiss sweet is made by boiling sugar and cream until it is light brown?
79465.e: For Rahmtäfeli, sugar is boiled with cream and butter. The sugar caramelises and turns the mixture brown.
79465.m: Rahmtäfeli are made from sugar and cream.

79466.q: Why does a cut apple with lemon juice turn brown more slowly?
a: The juice slows down the browning
79466.e: In the air, the flesh of the fruit turns brown. Lemon juice slows this change down.
79466.m: Lemon juice keeps apples pale for longer.

79467.q: Which vitamin is lemon juice especially rich in?
79467.e: Lemons are rich in vitamin C. The body needs it, for example, to fight off illness.
79467.m: Lemons contain a lot of vitamin C.

79468.q: What happens when you pour lemon juice into milk?
79468.e: The acid in the lemon makes the protein in the milk clump together. White flakes form.

79469.q: What happens to a dark, tarnished copper coin when you rub it with lemon juice and salt?
79469.e: The acid in lemon juice dissolves the dark layer on the coin. The shiny metal underneath appears again.
79469.m: Lemon juice makes dark copper shiny again.

79470.q: Where in a lemon is the strong-smelling oil?
79470.e: The lemon peel contains tiny oil glands. If you grate the peel, it smells strongly of lemon.
79470.m: The scented oil is in the lemon peel.

79471.q: What can you produce with a lemon, a piece of copper and a piece of zinc?
79471.e: The sour juice and the two metals together form a simple battery. It supplies a tiny bit of electricity.
79471.m: You can build a battery with a lemon.

79472.q: Which group of fruits does the lemon belong to?
79472.e: The lemon belongs to the citrus fruits. Oranges and mandarins are citrus fruits too.
79472.m: The lemon is a citrus fruit.

79473.q: What happens when you drip lemon juice onto a piece of limestone?
a: The stone goes soft like wax
79473.e: The acid in lemon juice attacks the limestone. This produces a gas that forms little bubbles.

79474.q: What happens when you pour sherbet powder into water?
79474.e: In water, the substances in the sherbet powder react with each other. This forms lots of gas bubbles.

79475.q: Which two substances in sherbet powder fizz together?
a: Bicarbonate of soda and an acid
79475.e: Sherbet powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid. Together with water they make gas.
79475.m: Bicarbonate of soda and acid make sherbet powder fizz.

79476.q: Which acid is often found in sherbet powder?
79476.e: Sherbet powder usually contains citric acid or tartaric acid. It also gives the slightly sour taste.
79476.m: Sherbet powder often contains citric acid.

79477.q: What do you feel when you sprinkle sherbet powder on your tongue?
79477.e: Saliva is moist. That is why the sherbet powder starts to fizz and tingle on your tongue.
79477.m: Sherbet powder tingles on the tongue.

79478.q: Why must sherbet powder be kept dry?
a: Otherwise it fizzes in the tin
79478.e: Moisture starts the reaction. Then the powder is used up before you put it in the glass.

79479.q: What is a pressed tablet that fizzes in water called?
79479.e: An effervescent tablet contains the same substances as sherbet powder. It is just pressed tightly together.

79480.e: Besides bicarbonate of soda and acid, sherbet powder contains sugar. It gives the sweet taste.

79481.q: Where does sherbet powder fizz faster, in warm or in cold water?
79481.e: In warm water, chemical reactions happen faster. That is why sherbet powder fizzes more strongly there and is finished sooner.
79481.m: Sherbet powder fizzes faster in warm water.

79482.e: Lactic acid bacteria eat the milk sugar. As they do, they make acid, and the milk goes sour.

79483.q: Which acid forms in soured milk?
79483.e: The bacteria turn the milk sugar into lactic acid. This acid gets its name from milk (Latin ‘lac’).
79483.m: Lactic acid forms in soured milk.

79484.q: How does milk change when it goes sour?
79484.e: The acid makes the protein in the milk curdle. That is why soured milk gets thicker.

79485.q: Which dairy product is made with the help of lactic acid bacteria?
79485.e: To make yoghurt, lactic acid bacteria are added to warm milk. They make the milk sour and thick.
79485.m: Yoghurt is made with lactic acid bacteria.

79486.q: Where does milk go sour fastest?
79486.e: Bacteria multiply quickly in the warmth. In the fridge they work only slowly.
79486.m: Milk goes sour quickly in the warmth.

79487.q: What does soured milk taste like?
79487.e: Soured milk contains lactic acid. That is why it tastes slightly sour.

79488.q: What do you get when you let soured, thick milk drain?
79488.e: As it drains, the liquid runs away. A thick, white mass is left behind: quark.
79488.m: Quark is made from soured milk.

79489.q: What is the yellowish liquid that separates from soured milk called?
79489.e: When milk curdles, a yellowish liquid separates off. This liquid is called whey.
79489.m: The liquid from curdled milk is called whey.

79490.q: What happens to egg white when it is cooked?
79490.e: Raw egg white is see-through and runny. The heat makes it white and firm.
79490.m: Cooked egg white turns white and firm.

79491.q: About how long do you boil a hard-boiled egg?
79491.e: A medium egg is hard after about 10 minutes in boiling water. A soft-boiled egg needs only about 5 minutes.
79491.m: A hard-boiled egg boils for about 10 minutes.

79492.q: Can you make a boiled egg raw again?
79492.e: When cooked, the egg white changes for ever. This change cannot be undone.
79492.m: A boiled egg never becomes raw again.

79493.q: How does a hard-boiled egg spin on the table?
79493.e: Everything inside a hard-boiled egg is solid, so it spins like a top. A raw egg wobbles because the inside sloshes about.
79493.m: A hard-boiled egg spins like a top.

79494.q: Why do you put eggs in cold water after boiling them?
a: So they take in more salt
79494.e: A hot egg keeps cooking even outside the pan. Cold water cools it down quickly.

79495.q: What does the yolk get if you boil an egg for far too long?
79495.e: If boiled too long, substances from the white and the yolk react with each other. This produces a greenish rim.
79495.m: Eggs boiled too long have a green rim.

79496.q: Why are eggs often pricked before boiling?
79496.e: There is a small air bubble inside an egg. Through the hole, the air can escape when heated, and the shell cracks less often.

79497.q: Which sets first when cooking, the egg white or the yolk?
79497.e: The egg white is on the outside and gets hot first. It also sets at a slightly lower temperature than the yolk.
79497.m: When cooking, the egg white sets first.

79498.q: Which cereal is popcorn made from?
79498.e: Popcorn is made from a special kind of maize. The kernels burst open when heated.

79499.q: What is inside a maize kernel that turns to steam when heated?
79499.e: Inside the kernel there is some water. When heated, it turns into hot steam.
79499.m: A maize kernel contains a little water.

79500.q: Why does a maize kernel burst open when heated?
a: The kernel is cut from the outside
The oil presses from the outside
79500.e: The steam inside the kernel presses harder and harder against the hard shell. At some point it suddenly splits open.
79500.m: Steam bursts the maize kernel open.

79501.q: What is the kind of maize used to make popcorn called?
79501.e: Popping corn has an especially hard shell. That is why enough pressure can build up inside.
79501.m: Popcorn is made from popping corn.

79502.q: Why does a maize kernel with a crack in its shell not pop properly?
79502.e: The steam can slowly escape through the crack. So no pressure builds up to burst the kernel.
79502.m: A kernel with a crack does not pop properly.

79503.q: What do you hear when popcorn pops in the pan?
79503.e: Each kernel bursts open with a small bang. That is why the pan keeps popping.
79503.m: Popcorn pops as it bursts open.

79504.q: How does a maize kernel change when it becomes popcorn?
79504.e: When it bursts, the soft inside of the kernel puffs up. The popcorn is much bigger than the kernel was before.
79504.m: Popcorn is much bigger than the maize kernel.

79505.q: Where does maize originally come from?
79505.e: Maize was first grown in Central America. Only later did it come to Europe.

79506.q: Why do you put a lid on the pan when making popcorn?
a: So the kernels don't jump out
79506.e: The bursting kernels jump up. With the lid they stay in the pan, and hot oil does not spatter out.
79506.m: A lid keeps the popcorn in the pan.

79507.q: Which parts of the sunflower is sunflower oil pressed from?
79507.e: Sunflower seeds contain a lot of oil. It is pressed out in an oil mill.
79507.m: Sunflower oil comes from the seeds.

79508.q: Which yellow-flowering field crop is most home-grown cooking oil in Switzerland pressed from?
79508.e: In spring, many rapeseed fields bloom yellow in Switzerland. Rapeseed oil is pressed from the small seeds.
79508.m: A lot of rapeseed oil is made in Switzerland.

79509.q: Which oil is made from the fruit of trees around the Mediterranean?
79509.e: Olive trees grow mainly around the Mediterranean. Olive oil is pressed from their fruit.

79510.q: What does a drop of oil leave on paper?
79510.e: Oil soaks into the paper and does not evaporate like water. That is why a see-through grease spot is left.
79510.m: Oil leaves a grease spot on paper.

79511.q: Why is cooking oil best kept in a dark, cool place?
79511.e: Light, warmth and air change the oil over time. Then it smells and tastes rancid.
79511.m: Keep cooking oil dark and cool.

79512.q: What does oil feel like between your fingers?
79512.e: Oil makes the skin smooth and slippery. That is why it feels slippery.

79513.q: Where should old cooking oil go?
79513.e: Oil blocks pipes and pollutes water. That is why you take it to a collection point in a bottle.
79513.m: Old oil goes to a collection point.

79514.q: What often happens to olive oil in the fridge?
79514.e: In the cold, some fats in olive oil go solid. That is why it goes cloudy and thick, but clear again when warm.
79514.m: Olive oil goes cloudy in the cold.

79515.e: Chips are deep-fried in hot oil. The oil is much hotter than boiling water and makes them crispy.
79515.m: Chips are fried in hot oil.

80405.q: What do you do with finely chopped red cabbage to get red cabbage juice?
80405.e: The hot water draws the colour out of the leaves. After cooling, you pour the coloured juice through a sieve.
80405.m: Hot water draws the colour out of red cabbage.

80406.q: What colour is red cabbage juice in pure water?
80406.e: In water that is neither acidic nor basic, red cabbage juice is purple. Only when you add something does the colour change.
80406.m: In pure water, red cabbage juice is purple.

80407.q: What colour does red cabbage juice turn when you stir in bicarbonate of soda?
80407.e: Bicarbonate of soda is not acidic but basic. That is why the purple red cabbage juice turns blue to blue-green.
80407.m: Bicarbonate of soda turns red cabbage juice blue.

80408.q: What does red cabbage juice show with its colour?
80408.e: The dye in red cabbage changes colour depending on whether a substance is acidic or basic. This lets you test things from the kitchen.
80408.m: Red cabbage juice shows by its colour whether something is acidic.

80409.q: What do you call a substance that shows by its colour whether something is acidic?
80409.e: An indicator is something that shows. Red cabbage juice is an indicator you can make yourself.
80409.m: An indicator shows by its colour whether something is acidic.

80410.q: What does a splash of vinegar do to the colour when cooking red cabbage?
80410.e: Acid from vinegar or sour apples keeps red cabbage red. Without acid it tends to turn bluish when cooked.
80410.m: With a little acid, cooked red cabbage stays red.

80411.q: What property does lemon juice have if it turns red cabbage juice red?
80411.e: Lemon juice contains acid. Acidic substances turn red cabbage juice red.
80411.m: Acidic substances turn red cabbage juice red.

80412.q: Which juice, like red cabbage juice, changes colour with acid?
80412.e: Blueberries contain a blue dye similar to red cabbage. That is why their juice also changes colour with acid.
80412.m: Blueberry juice also changes colour with acid.

80413.q: What is food colouring used for?
80413.e: Food colouring is safe to eat. It is used, for example, to colour cakes, icing or Easter eggs.

80414.q: Which colour do you get when you mix red and yellow food colouring?
80414.e: Red and yellow together make orange. This way you can mix many new colours from just a few.
80414.m: Red and yellow together make orange.

80415.q: Which vegetable colours food bright red?
80415.e: Beetroot contains a strong red dye. Hands and clothes quickly turn red from it too.

80416.e: Turmeric is a yellow powder made from a root. It colours curries yellow, for example.

80417.q: In which water does a drop of food colouring spread faster?
80417.e: In warm water the tiniest particles move faster. That is why the colour spreads more quickly there.
80417.m: Colour spreads faster in warm water than in cold.

80418.q: What happens to a white flower that stands in water with food colouring for a few days?
a: The flower loses all its leaves
The flower grows twice as big
80418.e: The flower sucks the coloured water up through its stem. This way the colour reaches the flower head.
80418.m: A flower sucks water up through its stem to the flower head.

80419.q: Which vegetable provides a green colouring for food?
80419.e: Spinach contains a lot of green leaf pigment. You can use spinach to colour pasta green, for example.

80420.q: Which letter do the numbers of colourings on packaging start with?
80420.e: Additives such as colourings have an E number on packaging. Colourings have the numbers E 100 to E 199.
80420.m: Colourings are listed on packaging with an E number.

80421.q: You want to separate the colours of a felt-tip pen with water. Which paper do you put the dot of colour on?
80421.e: Coffee filter paper soaks up water well. The water can travel upwards in it and carry the colours with it.
80421.m: To separate colours, you need paper that soaks up water well.

80422.q: A coffee filter with a felt-tip dot stands in water. What travels up the paper and takes the colour with it?
80422.e: The paper soaks water up from the glass. The water dissolves the colour and carries it along.
80422.m: The water carries the colours up the paper.

80423.q: You draw a dot with a black felt-tip pen on a coffee filter and stand it in water. What do you soon see?
a: No colour at all any more
80423.e: Black felt-tip ink is often mixed from several colours. On the paper they separate, for example into blue, yellow and red.
80423.m: Black ink is often mixed from several colours.

80424.q: Where must the dot of colour be on the paper strip when it goes into the water?
80424.e: If the dot is in the water, the colour simply dissolves in the glass. If it is just above, the water rises up to it.
80424.m: The dot of colour must be just above the water.

80425.q: Which pens can you use to separate colours in paper with water?
80425.e: The colour must dissolve in water, otherwise it just stays put. That is why washable felt-tip pens work best.
80425.m: To separate colours with water, you need washable felt-tip pens.

80426.q: What does the Greek word ‘chroma’ in chromatography mean?
80426.e: ‘Chroma’ is the Greek word for colour. So chromatography means roughly ‘colour writing’.

80427.q: A coffee filter with a felt-tip dot stands in water. Why do different stripes of colour appear?
80427.e: Some colours are easily carried along by the water, others tend to stay behind. So they get different distances and separate.
80427.m: Each colour travels a different distance in the paper.

80428.q: Which pigments can you separate from green leaves with chromatography?
80428.e: Green leaves contain not only green but also yellow pigment. With methylated spirits instead of water, and with the help of an adult, you can separate them.
80428.m: Green leaves also contain yellow pigment.

80429.q: What can you use to make a simple invisible ink?
80429.e: Lemon juice is almost colourless and hard to see once dry. That is why it works well as invisible ink.
80429.m: Lemon juice is a simple invisible ink.

80430.q: How do you make writing in lemon juice visible again?
80430.e: When the paper is carefully warmed, for example with an iron, the dried juice changes colour. Only do this with an adult.
80430.m: Heat makes secret writing in lemon juice visible.

80431.q: What colour does lemon juice writing turn when heated?
80431.e: The juice contains sugar and other substances. When heated they turn brown, a bit like toast.

80432.q: Which drink from the fridge can also be an invisible ink?
80432.e: Dried milk is hard to see on white paper. When carefully warmed it turns brown and the writing appears.
80432.m: Milk can also be used as invisible ink.

80433.q: You write with a white candle on white paper. How do you make the writing visible?
80433.e: Wax repels water. The watercolour stays on the paper but not on the wax letters, so they show up light.
80433.m: Wax repels watercolour, so candle writing appears.

80434.q: What is the best thing to write on paper with lemon juice?
80434.e: You dip a cotton bud or a fine brush into the lemon juice and write with it. A pen would leave visible lines.
80434.m: Secret writing in lemon juice is done with a cotton bud or brush.

80435.q: You write with bicarbonate of soda water and then brush red cabbage juice over it. What happens?
80435.e: The bicarbonate of soda changes the colour of the red cabbage juice. That is why the letters appear in a different colour from the rest of the paper.
80435.m: Red cabbage juice can make bicarbonate of soda writing visible.

80436.q: What did people use invisible ink for in the past?
80436.e: With invisible ink, messages could be hidden. Only those who knew how to make it visible could read them.
80436.m: Invisible ink hides messages from prying eyes.

80437.e: Soap is made by boiling fats or oils with an alkali. This boiling is called soap making.
80437.m: Soap is made from fat and alkali.

80438.q: Why do you wash your hands with soap instead of just water?
80438.e: Water alone is poor at rinsing away greasy dirt. Soap wraps up the grease so that the water can rinse it away.
80438.m: Soap helps water rinse away greasy dirt.

80439.q: You sprinkle pepper on water and dip in a finger covered in soap. What does the pepper do?
80439.e: The soap weakens the stretched skin on the surface of the water. The water pulls back towards the edge and takes the pepper with it.
80439.m: Soap weakens the skin on the water.

80440.q: What were the craftsmen who used to make soap called?
80440.e: Soap was boiled in large pots. That is why the craftsmen were called soap boilers.
80440.m: In the past, soap boilers boiled soap in large pots.

80441.q: What forms when you rub soap with a little water between your hands?
80441.e: Soap and water form lots of tiny bubbles when rubbed. You know this white lather from washing your hands.

80442.q: When should you wash your hands with soap especially well?
a: After the toilet and before eating
80442.e: After using the toilet and before eating, clean hands are especially important. That way fewer germs get into your mouth.
80442.m: Wash your hands with soap after the toilet and before eating.

80443.q: A little paper boat has a drop of soap at the back. What happens in the water?
80443.e: The soap weakens the skin on the water at the back. At the front the water pulls more strongly, so the boat moves forwards.
80443.m: A drop of soap can power a paper boat.

80444.q: What happens to a bar of soap that lies in a puddle of water for a long time?
80444.e: Water slowly dissolves the soap at its surface. That is why it is better to let soap dry after washing.
80444.m: Soap in water goes soft and slimy.

80445.q: What is a simple, unscented bar of soap that is also used to wash clothes called?
80445.e: Household soap is a simple, solid soap. It is used, for example, to wash stains out of clothes.
80445.m: Household soap is a simple solid soap.

80446.q: What shape is a soap bubble that floats freely through the air?
80446.e: The thin soap skin pulls itself together as small as possible. The shape with the smallest surface is the sphere.
80446.m: A freely floating soap bubble is perfectly round.

80447.q: What is inside a soap bubble?
80447.e: When you blow, you blow air into the soap skin. Only the thin skin is made of soapy water.
80447.m: A soap bubble is full of air.

80448.q: Why does a soap bubble shimmer in many colours?
a: Light is reflected in the thin skin
80448.e: Light is reflected from the front and back of the thin soap skin. This creates shimmering rainbow colours.
80448.m: The thin skin of a soap bubble makes rainbow colours.

80449.q: What do you add to soapy water so that soap bubbles last longer?
80449.e: Glycerine is a thick, clear liquid. It stops the soap skin from drying out so quickly.
80449.m: Glycerine makes soap bubbles last longer.

80450.q: Why does a soap bubble burst after a while?
80450.e: The water in the soap skin evaporates and flows downwards. When the skin gets too thin, the bubble bursts.
80450.m: A soap bubble bursts when its skin gets too thin.

80451.q: What often happens if you carefully poke a soap bubble with a wet, soapy finger?
80451.e: A dry finger makes the bubble burst. But a finger with soapy water joins up with the soap skin.
80451.m: You can touch a soap bubble with a wet, soapy finger.

80452.q: What can happen to a soap bubble in very cold weather?
80452.e: In hard frost, the water in the soap skin freezes. Then you can see delicate ice patterns on the bubble.
80452.m: In hard frost, soap bubbles can freeze.

80453.q: About how thick is the skin of a soap bubble?
80453.e: The skin of a soap bubble is wafer-thin. It is much thinner than a human hair.
80453.m: The skin of a soap bubble is wafer-thin.

80454.q: What do you mix to make a simple bubble mixture?
80454.e: For soap bubbles you need water and something soapy such as washing-up liquid. Together they make a stretchy skin.
80454.m: Water and washing-up liquid make a bubble mixture.

80455.e: Foam is made of lots of bubbles full of air. Between the bubbles are thin walls of liquid.
80455.m: Foam is made of lots of little air bubbles.

80456.q: Which foam do you get when you beat egg white hard?
80456.e: When beating, air is stirred into the egg white. It turns white and stiff and is then called whisked egg white.
80456.m: Beaten egg white is called whisked egg white.

80457.q: What do you whip to make whipped cream?
80457.e: When whipping, air gets into the cream. The fat in the cream holds the bubbles in place.
80457.m: Whipping cream turns it into whipped cream.

80458.q: What do firefighters often use to put out burning petrol?
80458.e: The foam lies over the burning petrol like a blanket. Then no more air can reach the fire.

a: It contains a lot of flour
80459.e: Each bubble reflects a little light in all directions. Together the many bubbles look white, much like snow.
80459.m: Lots of little bubbles make foam look white.

80460.q: Where can you find solid foam?
80460.e: Foam rubber is solid foam with lots of air bubbles. That is why a mattress is soft and light.
80460.m: Foam rubber is solid foam full of air.

80461.q: Which drink often has a layer of milk froth on top?
80461.e: For a cappuccino, milk is frothed up with hot steam. The froth goes on top of the coffee.
80461.m: A cappuccino has milk froth on top.

80462.q: What happens to foam if you wait a long time?
80462.e: The thin walls of the bubbles get thinner over time and burst. That is why foam slowly sinks down.

80463.q: Why do you put washing-up liquid in the washing-up water?
a: It loosens the grease from the dishes
80463.e: Grease sticks to dishes and is hard to wash off with water alone. Washing-up liquid loosens the grease so the water can rinse it away.
80463.m: Washing-up liquid loosens grease from dishes.

80464.q: What happens if you add a little washing-up liquid to milk with drops of colour?
80464.e: The washing-up liquid changes the surface of the milk and loosens the milk fat. This sets the colours moving.
80464.m: Washing-up liquid sets drops of colour on milk moving.

80465.q: Why must ordinary washing-up liquid not go into the dishwasher?
a: It makes far too much foam
80465.e: Washing-up liquid foams a lot. In the machine the foam would pour out, so it needs its own product.
80465.m: Only dishwasher detergent goes into the dishwasher.

80466.q: You drip water onto a coin. What changes if there is washing-up liquid in the water?
a: Many more drops fit on it
80466.e: Pure water forms a high dome on the coin. Washing-up liquid weakens the skin of the water, so it overflows sooner.
80466.m: With washing-up liquid, water does not form such a high dome.

80467.q: What must you never do with washing-up liquid?
80467.e: Washing-up liquid is for cleaning, not for eating or drinking. Keep it where small children cannot reach it.

80468.q: How much washing-up liquid do you need for a bowl of washing-up water?
80468.e: Washing-up liquid works even in small amounts. Too much is unnecessary and pollutes the waste water.
80468.m: A few squirts of washing-up liquid are enough for the washing-up.

80469.q: Why should you put cream on your hands after a long time washing up?
a: Washing-up liquid dries out the skin
Washing-up liquid makes the skin hot
Washing-up liquid makes the skin thick
80469.e: Washing-up liquid removes not only grease from dishes but also the skin's natural oils. A cream gives the skin back its oils.
80469.m: Washing-up liquid can dry out the skin.

80471.q: What happens when you shake a bottle of oil and water hard?
80471.e: When shaken, the oil breaks up into lots of tiny droplets that float in the water. The liquid then looks cloudy.
80471.m: When shaken, oil in water breaks up into tiny droplets.

80472.q: What must you never use to put out burning oil in a pan?
80472.e: Water sinks under the hot oil, turns to steam at once and throws burning oil out. It is better to smother the fire with a lid.
80472.m: Never put out burning oil with water.

80473.q: Which sauce is made from oil and egg yolk that mix well?
80473.e: Egg yolk contains a substance that joins oil and water. That is why oil and egg yolk become a thick mayonnaise.
80473.m: Mayonnaise is a mixture of oil and egg yolk.

80474.q: In which drink are tiny droplets of fat spread through water?
80474.e: Milk is mostly water. Tiny droplets of fat float in it, which is why it is white and not see-through.
80474.m: Tiny droplets of fat float in milk.

80475.q: What do you call a mixture of tiny oil droplets in water?
80475.e: An emulsion is a mixture of two liquids that do not normally mix. One floats in tiny droplets in the other.
80475.m: A mixture of oil droplets in water is called an emulsion.

80476.q: What helps oil and water mix better?
80476.e: Washing-up liquid can cling to oil and to water at the same time. In this way it joins the two liquids.
80476.m: Washing-up liquid helps oil and water mix.

80477.q: Why can't you wash an oil stain out of a jumper with water alone?
a: Oil is too cold for it
80477.e: Water simply runs off the oil in beads. You need soap or detergent to loosen the oil.
80477.m: Wash oil stains with soap, not just with water.

80478.q: What do you do with a salad dressing of oil and vinegar just before serving?
80478.e: Oil and vinegar separate when the dressing stands. Shaking or stirring mixes them again.
80478.m: Shake a salad dressing well before serving.

80479.q: What makes the lumps of wax in a lava lamp rise?
80479.e: At the bottom of the lava lamp is a light bulb. It warms the wax, which expands, gets lighter and rises.
80479.m: In a lava lamp, heat makes the wax rise.

80480.q: What happens to the wax at the top of a lava lamp?
80480.e: It is cooler at the top than at the bottom. The wax cools, becomes heavier again and sinks back down.
80480.m: Cooled wax sinks down in a lava lamp.

80481.q: What do you see in a lava lamp?
a: Coloured blobs floating up and down
80481.e: In a lava lamp, soft, coloured blobs of wax float slowly upwards and back down again.
80481.m: In a lava lamp, blobs of wax float up and down.

80482.q: What makes the bubbles rise in a home-made lava lamp of water and oil?
80482.e: The effervescent tablet fizzes in the water and forms gas bubbles. These carry coloured drops of water upwards.
80482.m: An effervescent tablet makes a home-made lava lamp bubble.

80483.q: What does the food colouring colour in a home-made lava lamp of water and oil?
80483.e: Food colouring dissolves in water but not in oil. That is why the oil stays clear and only the water becomes coloured.
80483.m: Food colouring colours water but not oil.

80484.q: Why does it take a while for a real lava lamp to start bubbling after it is switched on?
a: The wax has to warm up first
The water has to freeze first
The lamp has to dry first
80484.e: At first the wax is solid and cold. Only when it is warm and soft do the blobs start to rise.
80484.m: A lava lamp needs time for the wax to warm up.

80485.q: Why should you not shake a warm lava lamp?
80485.e: When shaken, wax and liquid mix into tiny droplets. The lamp can then stay cloudy for a long time.
80485.m: Never shake a warm lava lamp.

80486.q: Where does the lava lamp get its name from?
a: It is filled with real lava
It was invented on a volcano
It gets as hot as lava
80486.e: The slowly flowing blobs of wax look like glowing lava from a volcano. That is why it is called a lava lamp.
80486.m: The wax blobs in a lava lamp look like lava.

80487.q: What can you easily use to grow crystals at home?
80487.e: You dissolve a lot of salt or sugar in water. As the water slowly evaporates, crystals grow from it.
80487.m: You can grow crystals from salt water or sugar water.

80488.q: Why do you dissolve the salt in warm water to grow crystals?
a: The salt turns colourful in it
The salt turns sweet in it
The salt goes hard in it
80488.e: Warm water can take up more salt than cold. The more salt is dissolved, the better the crystals grow.
80488.m: More salt dissolves in warm water.

80489.q: What do you hang in the salt solution so that crystals grow on it?
80489.e: You tie a piece of string to a pencil and lay the pencil across the glass. The crystals form on the string.
80489.m: Crystals grow on a string in the salt solution.

80490.q: How long does it take for nice crystals to grow?
80490.e: Crystals grow slowly while the water evaporates. So you need patience and should check every day.
80490.m: Growing crystals takes several days of patience.

80491.q: Where is the best place to put the glass with the crystal solution?
80491.e: Crystals grow best when the glass is not moved. Shaking disturbs their growth.
80491.m: Crystals grow best in a quiet place.

80492.q: What are the large sugar crystals you can put in tea called?
80492.e: Rock sugar forms when sugar slowly crystallises out of a solution. This produces large, clear crystals.
80492.m: Rock sugar is made of large sugar crystals.

80493.q: How many arms does a snow crystal have?
80493.e: Snow crystals are ice crystals. Because of the way ice is built, snowflakes have six arms or six points.
80493.m: A snow crystal has six arms.

80495.q: What is rock crystal made of?
80495.e: Rock crystal is clear, transparent quartz. Especially beautiful pieces are found in the Swiss Alps.
80495.m: Rock crystal is made of quartz.

80496.q: What colour is table salt in the tub?
80496.e: A single pure salt crystal is actually transparent. Lots of small grains together look white.

80497.q: Why did people in the past put meat and fish in salt?
80497.e: Salt draws water out of food. Without water, bacteria can hardly multiply, so salted food goes off less quickly.
80497.m: Salt makes meat and fish keep longer.

80498.q: Which animals like to lick a salt lick in the barn?
80498.e: Cows need salt, but they find too little of it in grass. That is why they get a salt lick in the barn or in the field.
80498.m: Cows like to lick a salt lick.

80499.q: Which bake is often sprinkled with coarse grains of salt?
80499.e: Pretzels are sprinkled with coarse salt before baking. The other bakes are usually sweet or have no salt crust.
80499.m: Pretzels are sprinkled with coarse salt.

80500.q: What is salt that is mined deep in the earth called?
80500.e: A very long time ago, seas dried up and left layers of salt behind. This salt in the ground is called rock salt.
80500.m: Salt from the earth is called rock salt.

80501.q: What do you use to sprinkle salt on your food at the table?
80501.e: A salt cellar has little holes at the top. That way only a little salt lands on the food.
80501.m: You season food at the table with a salt cellar.

80502.q: How much salt should you use with your food?
80502.e: The body needs some salt. But too much salt is unhealthy, so use it sparingly.

81381.e: Wood is the hard material in the trunk and branches of trees. Trees are felled and sawn into planks.
81381.m: Wood grows in the trees of the forest.

81382.q: What can you tell from the rings in a tree trunk?
81382.e: A tree forms a new annual ring every year. If you count the rings, you know how old the tree is.
81382.m: Each annual ring stands for one year of the tree's life.

81383.q: What does a dry piece of wood do in water?
81383.e: Dry wood is lighter than the same amount of water. That is why it floats on top.

81384.q: What is the craftsperson who makes furniture from wood called?
81384.e: The joiner saws, planes and glues wood into tables, cupboards and doors.
81384.m: A joiner makes furniture from wood.

81385.q: Which conifer in Switzerland loses its needles in autumn?
81385.e: In autumn the larch turns its needles golden yellow and drops them. Larch wood is very hard and lasts a long time outdoors.
81385.m: The larch has no needles in winter.

81386.q: What do Swiss wrestlers (Schwinger) fight on?
81386.e: Sawdust is produced when wood is sawn. It is soft and protects the wrestlers when they fall.
81386.m: In Swiss wrestling, soft sawdust covers the ring.

81387.q: Which tree grows most often in Swiss forests?
81387.e: The spruce is the most common tree in Swiss forests. Its wood is often used for building.
81387.m: The spruce is the most common tree in Swiss forests.

81388.q: Why doesn't a wooden spoon in a hot pan get as hot as a metal spoon?
81388.e: Wood passes on heat only very slowly. That is why you can easily hold a wooden spoon.

81389.q: What happens to wood that stays wet for a long time?
81389.e: Fungi and tiny living things break down wet wood. It becomes soft and crumbly.

81390.q: What is glass mainly made from?
81390.e: Glass is made mainly from quartz sand. It is heated very strongly with other substances and melted.
81390.m: Glass is made from melted sand.

81391.q: About how hot does it have to be to melt glass?
81391.e: To melt sand into glass, you need a furnace at well over 1000 degrees. That is much hotter than an oven.
81391.m: Glass is only made in very great heat.

81392.q: What often happens when a drinking glass falls on a hard floor?
81392.e: Glass is hard but brittle. A hard knock breaks it into pieces.
81392.m: Glass is hard, but it breaks easily.

81393.q: What is a craftsperson called who shapes hot glass into vases using a pipe?
81393.e: The glassblower picks up liquid glass on a long pipe. Then they blow into it, and the glass becomes a ball or a vase.
81393.m: A glassblower shapes vases with their breath.

81394.q: Which part of a house is usually made of glass?
81394.e: Window panes are made of glass so that light comes into the house. Wind and rain stay outside.
81394.m: Light comes into the house through glass window panes.

81395.q: Why should you not pick up broken glass with your bare hands?
81395.e: The edges of broken glass are as sharp as a knife. It is better to sweep it up with a dustpan and brush.

81396.q: What happens to glass when it is heated very strongly?
81396.e: In great heat, glass becomes soft and thick like honey. Then it can be shaped.
81396.m: Hot glass becomes soft and can be shaped.

81397.q: What is behind the glass of a mirror?
81397.e: On the back of the mirror glass is a very thin layer of silver or aluminium. It reflects the light.
81397.m: A mirror has a shiny layer of metal at the back.

81398.q: What are colourful marbles for playing often made of?
81398.e: Many marbles are little balls of coloured glass.
81398.m: Many marbles are made of coloured glass.
