81399.q: Why are railway tracks made of steel?
a: Steel is very strong and hard
81399.e: Steel is a very strong metal. The rails have to carry heavy trains without breaking.

81400.q: What does a piece of metal usually feel like when you touch it?
81400.e: Metal quickly carries the warmth of your hand away. That is why it feels cool.
81400.m: Metal feels cool because it carries heat away quickly.

81401.q: Why is there a metal wire inside an electric cable?
81401.e: Electricity flows well through metals such as copper. That is why the wires in cables are made of metal.

81402.q: What happens to metal in very great heat?
81402.e: If metal is heated strongly enough, it becomes liquid. Then it can be poured into moulds.
81402.m: In great heat, metal becomes liquid.

81403.q: What does freshly polished metal look like?
81403.e: Metals reflect a lot of light. That is why they shine when they are clean and polished.
81403.m: Polished metal shines in the light.

81404.q: Which device can you use to find metal hidden in the ground?
81404.e: A metal detector beeps when there is metal underneath it. This is how you find coins or nails in the ground.
81404.m: A metal detector beeps at metal in the ground.

a: A long thin thread of metal
81405.e: A wire is metal that has been drawn out long and thin. You can bend it.
81405.m: A wire is a thin thread of metal.

81406.q: What are most metals obtained from?
81406.e: Ore is a rock that contains metal. It is melted in a furnace to get the metal out.
81406.m: Metals are obtained from ore in rock.

81407.q: What are forks and knives usually made of?
81407.e: Cutlery is usually made of stainless steel. This is a metal that is strong and does not rust.
81407.m: Cutlery is usually made of stainless steel.

81409.q: What is plastic usually made from?
81409.e: Most plastics are made in factories from crude oil.
81409.m: Most plastics are made from crude oil.

81410.q: What is a good property of plastic?
a: It is light and easy to shape
It is as heavy as iron
81410.e: Plastic is light and can be shaped into almost any form. That is why boxes, toys and much more are made from it.
81410.m: Plastic is light and easy to shape.

81411.q: Why is plastic a problem in nature?
81411.e: Plastic does not rot like leaves. It stays in nature for many hundreds of years.
81411.m: Plastic stays in nature for a very long time.

81412.q: Does plastic grow in nature or is it made by people?
81412.e: Plastic is a synthetic, man-made material. People make it in factories.
81412.m: Plastic is a man-made material from the factory.

81413.q: Which object is usually made of plastic?
81413.e: The handle and bristles of a toothbrush are usually made of plastic. It is light and does not get soggy.
81413.m: Most toothbrushes are made of plastic.

81414.q: What happens to many plastics when they get very hot?
81414.e: Many plastics go soft in the heat and melt. That is why you don't put plastic on a hot hob.
81414.m: Many plastics go soft in the heat.

81415.q: What are fleece jumpers usually made of?
81415.e: Fleece is made of fine plastic fibres. The fabric is light, soft and warm.
81415.m: Fleece is a warm fabric made of plastic fibres.

81416.q: Why is there a plastic coating around an electric cable?
81416.e: Plastic does not let electricity through. The coating protects us when we touch the cable.
81416.m: A plastic coating protects us from electricity.

81417.q: What is paper usually made from?
81417.e: To make paper, wood is broken down into fine fibres. These are mixed with water and pressed into thin sheets.
81417.m: Paper is usually made from wood fibres.

81418.q: What did the ancient Egyptians write on before there was paper?
81418.e: Papyrus was made from the stems of a plant by the Nile. Our word paper comes from it.
81418.m: The ancient Egyptians wrote on papyrus.

81419.q: What do you call thick, stiff paper for boxes?
81419.e: Cardboard is much thicker and stiffer than writing paper. Boxes and packaging are made from it.
81419.m: Boxes are often made of stiff cardboard.

81420.q: What can be made again from waste paper?
81420.e: The fibres in waste paper can be used again. That way less wood is needed for new paper.
81420.m: New paper is made from waste paper.

81421.q: Why must paper not be near a burning candle?
81421.e: Paper is thin and dry. It burns very quickly even from a small flame.

81422.q: Where does natural rubber come from?
a: From the sap of a tree
81422.e: Natural rubber is made from the milky sap of the rubber tree. The bark is cut and the sap is collected.
81422.m: Natural rubber comes from the sap of the rubber tree.

a: It is as hard as stone
81423.e: You can pull and squeeze rubber. Afterwards it goes back to its old shape.

81424.q: What do you use a rubber for?
81424.e: A rubber rubs pencil marks off the paper. That is where its name comes from.
81424.m: You remove pencil marks with a rubber.

81425.q: Why do people like wearing wellies in the rain?
a: Rubber does not let water through
81425.e: Rubber is waterproof. In wellies your feet stay dry even in puddles.

81426.q: What is the milky sap of the rubber tree called?
81426.e: The white sap of the rubber tree is called latex. Natural rubber is made from it.
81426.m: The sap of the rubber tree is called latex.

81427.q: Where does the rubber tree originally grow?
81427.e: The rubber tree comes from the rainforest by the Amazon. Today it is grown mainly in Asia.
81427.m: The rubber tree comes from the Amazon rainforest.

81428.q: What is a balloon usually made of?
81428.e: Balloons are usually made of thin rubber. That is why you can blow them up big.
81428.m: A balloon is made of thin rubber.

81429.q: Which part of a trainer is usually made of rubber?
81429.e: A rubber sole does not slip easily. It is springy and lasts a long time.
81429.m: Rubber soles don't slip so easily.

81430.q: Which animal does most wool come from?
81430.e: Sheep have a thick, curly coat. Wool is made from it.

81431.q: What do you do with wool to turn it into a thread?
81431.e: When spinning, the wool fibres are twisted into a long thread. In the past this was done with a spinning wheel.
81431.m: Wool is spun into a thread.

81432.q: What do you use to knit a woolly jumper?
81432.e: With two knitting needles, the wool is looped into stitches. Row by row, a piece of fabric grows.
81432.m: Knitting needles turn wool into stitches.

81433.q: Why does a woolly jumper keep you so nice and warm?
a: It traps a lot of air
81433.e: A lot of air gets caught between the curly wool fibres. This air holds in the body's warmth.
81433.m: The air in wool keeps us warm.

81434.q: Which animal from South America also gives very fine wool?
81434.e: Alpacas come from the Andes. Their wool is soft and warm, and there are alpacas on Swiss farms too.
81434.m: The alpaca gives soft, fine wool.

81435.q: What can happen to a woolly jumper if you wash it too hot?
81435.e: In hot water with lots of rubbing, the wool fibres mat together. The jumper shrinks and gets smaller.
81435.m: Wash wool cool, otherwise it shrinks.

81436.q: What is a thick fabric made of tightly pressed wool called?
81436.e: To make felt, wet wool is pressed and rubbed until the fibres hold firmly together. Slippers, for example, are made from it.
81436.m: Felt is made from pressed wool.

81437.q: Which part of the cotton plant provides the fibres?
81437.e: The seeds of the plant are surrounded by white, fluffy hairs. These hairs are picked and spun into yarn.
81437.m: Cotton fibres grow on the seeds of the plant.

81438.q: Why is cotton not grown in fields in Switzerland?
a: It is too cold for it
81438.e: Cotton needs a lot of warmth and a long warm season each year. Switzerland is too cool for it.
81438.m: Cotton only grows in warm countries.

81439.q: Which trousers are usually made of cotton?
81439.e: Jeans are made of a strong cotton fabric. It is usually dyed blue.
81439.m: Jeans are made of strong cotton fabric.

81440.q: Why do people like wearing cotton T-shirts in summer?
81440.e: Cotton is soft and soaks up moisture well. That is why it feels pleasant on the skin.

81441.q: What are the little sticks with soft cotton tips at both ends called?
81441.e: Cotton wool is made from cotton. Cotton buds are used, for example, for crafts or personal care.
81441.m: Cotton buds have tips of soft cotton wool.

81442.q: Which city in eastern Switzerland became world-famous for embroidery on cotton fabric?
81442.e: Over 100 years ago, much of the world's embroidery came from the St Gallen area. It was often stitched onto fine cotton fabrics.
81442.m: St Gallen is famous for its embroidery.

81443.q: What colour are cotton fibres usually?
81443.e: Cotton on the plant looks like white cotton wool balls. Coloured fabrics are only dyed later.

81444.e: Clay is a fine, damp earth. It is easy to knead and shape.

81445.q: What do you do with shaped clay to make it really hard?
a: You fire it in a kiln
81445.e: In a very hot kiln, the clay becomes as hard as stone. Only then is it ceramics.
81445.m: Clay is fired hard in a kiln.

81446.q: What is the craftsperson who makes crockery from clay called?
81446.e: The potter shapes cups, plates and jugs from clay and then fires them.
81446.m: The potter makes crockery from clay.

81447.q: On which spinning disc are round pots shaped?
81447.e: The potter's wheel spins fast. With their hands, the potter pulls the clay up into a round pot.
81447.m: Round pots are shaped on the potter's wheel.

81448.q: What is the fine white ceramic for beautiful cups called?
81448.e: Porcelain is an especially fine and hard ceramic. It is white and sometimes almost translucent.

81449.q: What are bathroom tiles usually made of?
81449.e: Tiles are fired ceramic slabs. They are hard and easy to clean with water.
81449.m: Bathroom tiles are usually made of ceramic.

81450.q: What is the shiny layer on ceramic crockery called?
81450.e: The glaze is a thin, glass-like layer. It makes the crockery smooth, shiny and watertight.
81450.m: A glaze makes ceramics smooth and shiny.

81451.q: What are red roof tiles usually made of?
81451.e: Roof tiles are shaped from clay and fired in a kiln. They keep out rain and snow for many years.
81451.m: Red roof tiles are made of fired clay.

81452.e: Leather is animal skin that has been specially treated. This makes it last and stops it rotting.
81452.m: Leather is made from animal skin.

81453.q: What do you call turning animal skin into leather?
81453.e: In tanning, the skin is treated with special substances. Afterwards it is soft, strong and long-lasting.

81454.q: What is the craftsperson who makes and mends shoes called?
81454.e: The shoemaker, also called a cobbler, often works with leather. They sew shoes and replace old soles.

81455.q: Which object is often made of leather?
81455.e: Leather is strong and flexible at the same time. That is why belts, bags and shoes are often made from it.
81455.m: Many belts are made of leather.

81456.q: Which animal does most of the world's leather come from?
81456.e: Most leather is made from the skin of cattle. The skin is thick and large.

81457.q: What do you use to look after leather shoes so that they shine?
81457.e: Shoe polish makes the leather soft and protects it from wet. After polishing, the shoes shine.
81457.m: Shoe polish cares for leather and makes it shine.

81458.q: What was the outer cover of a football made of in the past?
81458.e: In the past, footballs were sewn from pieces of leather. Today they are mostly made of plastic.
81458.m: Old footballs were sewn from leather.

81459.q: What lies on a horse's back when riding and is often made of leather?
81459.e: The saddle is usually made of strong leather. The rider sits on it safely and comfortably.
81459.m: A saddle is usually made of leather.

81460.e: For concrete, cement, sand, gravel and water are mixed. After a while the mixture becomes rock hard.
81460.m: Concrete is made of cement, gravel and water.

81461.q: What happens to fresh concrete after a while?
81461.e: The cement combines with the water. This makes the concrete as hard as stone.
81461.m: Fresh concrete becomes rock hard over time.

81462.q: Which vehicle with a turning drum brings concrete to the building site?
81462.e: The drum of the cement mixer turns while it drives. This keeps the concrete liquid until it arrives.
81462.m: The cement mixer turns its drum while driving.

81463.q: What is put into concrete to make it even stronger?
81463.e: Steel bars in concrete make it very strong. This is called reinforced concrete.
81463.m: Steel bars make concrete even stronger.

81464.q: Which ancient people already knew a kind of concrete?
81464.e: The Romans built with a kind of concrete about 2000 years ago. One example is the huge dome of the Pantheon in Rome.
81464.m: Even the Romans built with a kind of concrete.

81465.e: Cement is a fine grey powder. Mixed with water it goes hard and holds sand and gravel together.
81465.m: Cement is a grey powder that goes hard with water.

81466.q: Which vehicle brings liquid concrete to the building site?
81466.e: The cement mixer has a big drum at the back. It turns so that the concrete doesn't go hard on the way.
81466.m: The cement mixer brings the concrete to the building site.

81467.e: Bees sweat out tiny flakes of wax from their bodies. They build their home from them.

81468.q: What do bees build from wax?
81468.e: Honeycombs are made of many six-sided cells of wax. Honey and pollen are stored in them.
81468.m: Bees build their honeycombs from wax.

81469.q: What is most candle wax made from today?
81469.e: Most candles are made of paraffin wax. This wax is made from crude oil.
81469.m: Most candles are made of paraffin wax.

81470.q: What happens to liquid wax when it cools down?
81470.e: Wax goes liquid in the warmth. When it cools down, it goes solid again.
81470.m: Liquid wax goes solid as it cools.

81471.q: What are some wheels of cheese coated with on the outside?
81471.e: A layer of wax protects the cheese from drying out and from mould. You don't eat it.
81471.m: Wax protects some cheeses from drying out.

81472.q: What do you rub on the underside of skis so that they glide better?
81472.e: Ski wax makes the underside of the skis smooth. Then they glide better over the snow.
81472.m: With ski wax, skis glide better.

81473.q: What is the thread in the middle of a candle called?
81473.e: The wick draws liquid wax upwards. There it burns with a flame.
81473.m: A candle's wick draws wax upwards.

81474.q: What do you call dipping a wick again and again into liquid wax?
81474.e: In candle dipping, the candle gets a little thicker with each dip. In Switzerland, people like to do this during Advent.
81474.m: In candle dipping, the candle gets thicker layer by layer.

81475.q: What does a layer of wax do to water on a surface?
a: It makes it run off in beads
81475.e: Wax does not like water. The drops run off in beads and don't soak in.
81475.m: Water drops run off wax in beads.

82358.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns back into liquid water?
82358.e: When warm water vapour cools, little drops of water form again. This process is called condensation.
82358.m: In condensation, vapour turns back into water.

82359.q: What are the clouds in the sky made of?
a: Tiny drops of water and ice
82359.e: Clouds form when moist air rises and cools. This forms tiny drops of water or ice crystals.
82359.m: Clouds are made of very small drops of water or ice crystals.

82360.q: What are the drops of water that form on the grass early in the morning called?
82360.e: In the cool night, water vapour from the air turns into drops on the blades of grass. These drops are called dew.
82360.m: In the morning, dew often sparkles on the meadow.

82361.q: Why does a glass with an ice-cold drink get wet on the outside?
a: Water from the air settles on it
The glass has a tiny hole
The drink pushes through the glass
82361.e: The air contains invisible water vapour. On the cold glass it turns into drops.
82361.m: Drops of water from the air form on cold objects.

82362.q: Why do your glasses steam up in winter when you come into a warm house?
a: Warm, moist air cools on the cold lenses
The glasses get dirty in the house
The lenses go soft in the warmth
There is more dust in the house
82362.e: The glasses are still cold from outside. The warm room air cools on them, and its water vapour turns into tiny drops.
82362.m: Cold glasses steam up in a warm room.

82363.q: Why is the inside of the window panes often wet on cold winter mornings?
a: Moist room air cools on the glass
The cleaning cloth was too wet
82363.e: The warm air in the room contains water vapour. It cools on the cold pane, and drops form.
82363.m: Moisture collects on cold window panes.

82364.q: What are the white lines that aeroplanes draw high up in the sky called?
82364.e: The exhaust from the engines contains water vapour. In the freezing cold high up, it turns into tiny ice crystals that you see as lines.
82364.m: Condensation trails are made of tiny ice crystals.

82365.q: Why does water drip from the pipe of an air conditioner in summer?
a: Moisture from the air turns to water inside it
The unit is filled with water
The water comes from the rain
82365.e: In the air conditioner, the warm air is cooled down a lot. Its water vapour turns into water that has to drain away.
82365.m: When air cools a lot, its vapour turns into water.

82366.q: What is it called when water slowly turns into invisible vapour without boiling?
82366.e: Even without boiling, water particles are constantly passing into the air. This slow process is called evaporation.
82366.m: Water can evaporate even without boiling.

82368.q: Why do you feel cold when you climb out of the swimming pool wet?
a: The water on your skin evaporates and cools you
There are little bits of ice in the water
82368.e: Water needs heat to evaporate. It takes this heat from our skin, which is why we feel cold.

82369.q: Which cycle begins with water evaporating from seas and lakes?
82369.e: The evaporated water rises, forms clouds and falls back down as rain or snow. In this way the water keeps going round in a circle.
82369.m: In the water cycle, water travels between the earth and the sky.

82370.q: What provides most of the energy for water to evaporate from the sea?
82370.e: The sun warms the sea and the air. This makes a huge amount of water evaporate every day.
82370.m: The sun drives the evaporation of water.

82371.q: Why do people sometimes put a bowl of water on the radiator in winter?
a: To make the room air moister
82371.e: The warmth makes the water in the bowl evaporate. This puts more moisture into the dry heated air.
82371.m: Evaporating water makes dry air moister.

82372.q: How is salt obtained from seawater by the sea?
a: The water is left to evaporate in the sun
The water is shaken for a long time
The water is poured through a sieve
82372.e: In shallow pools, the sun and wind dry the seawater. The water goes into the air and the salt is left behind.
82372.m: When seawater evaporates, salt is left behind.

82373.q: How does a wet bath towel dry faster?
82373.e: Spread out, the towel has a large surface where water can go into the air. Scrunched up, it stays damp for a long time.
82373.m: A large surface makes water evaporate faster.

82374.q: On a high mountain, does water boil at more or less than 100 degrees?
a: It doesn't boil there at all
82374.e: On a mountain, less air presses down on the water. That is why it boils at a lower heat, for example at a mountain hut in the Alps.
82374.m: The higher you are, the sooner water boils.

82375.q: Which device do you use to measure how hot the water is?
82375.e: A thermometer shows the temperature. In Switzerland it is measured in degrees Celsius.
82375.m: You measure temperature with a thermometer.

a: The temperature at which something boils
The temperature at which something freezes
The highest point of a mountain
The point in the middle of the pan
82376.e: At the boiling point, a liquid starts to boil. For water at sea level, this is 100 degrees Celsius.
82376.m: At the boiling point, a liquid starts to boil.

82377.q: Who is the temperature unit degree Celsius named after?
82377.e: Anders Celsius was a scientist from Sweden. Almost 300 years ago he suggested a scale with 100 steps between water freezing and boiling.
82377.m: The Celsius scale is named after Anders Celsius.

82378.q: What happens to boiling water in an open pan if you turn the hob up even higher?
82378.e: The extra heat only makes more water turn to steam. But the temperature of the water does not rise above the boiling point.
82378.m: Boiling water does not get hotter, it just turns to steam faster.

82379.q: Why does water come to the boil faster with a lid on the pan?
a: The lid keeps the heat in the pan
The lid makes the water salty
The lid squeezes the water smaller
82379.e: Without a lid, a lot of heat escapes with the steam. With a lid, the heat stays in the pan, and you save energy too.
82379.m: With a lid, water boils faster and you save electricity.

82380.q: Which kitchen appliance boils water for tea especially quickly?
82380.e: In a kettle, a heating element warms the water directly. It switches itself off when the water boils.

82381.q: What is a pan with a tightly sealed lid, in which food cooks much faster, called?
82381.e: In a pressure cooker the steam cannot escape, so the pressure rises. This means the water only boils above 100 degrees, and the food cooks faster.
82381.m: It gets hotter in a pressure cooker than in an open pan.

82382.q: What happens to a puddle when it is minus 5 degrees outside?
82382.e: Minus 5 degrees is colder than the freezing point of water. That is why the puddle turns to ice.
82382.m: Below 0 degrees, a puddle turns to ice.

82383.q: Where in the kitchen do you keep food at about minus 18 degrees?
82383.e: A freezer keeps food at about minus 18 degrees. That way it keeps for a long time.
82383.m: It is much colder in the freezer than in the fridge.

82384.q: What are the balls of ice that sometimes fall from the sky in a thunderstorm called?
82384.e: In a thundercloud, drops of water freeze into balls of ice. When they fall, this is called hail.
82384.m: Hail is balls of ice from a thundercloud.

82385.q: Why should you never touch an ice-cold metal pole with your tongue in winter?
a: Your tongue can freeze to it
82385.e: The moist tongue cools down instantly on the ice-cold metal. The moisture freezes and the tongue sticks fast.

82386.q: What does it mean when the thermometer shows ‘minus 10 degrees’?
82386.e: The minus shows temperatures below zero. So minus 10 degrees is 10 degrees colder than 0 degrees.
82386.m: Minus degrees are colder than zero degrees.

82387.q: Why do people put antifreeze in the water for the car windscreen in winter?
82387.e: With antifreeze, the water only freezes at much lower temperatures. So you can clean the windscreen in winter too.

82388.q: What do you call it when rain freezes at once into a slippery layer of ice on the cold ground?
82388.e: When rain falls on ground colder than 0 degrees, it turns to ice at once. Then roads and pavements are very slippery.
82388.m: With black ice, the pavement is very slippery.

82389.q: What do you call weather with temperatures below 0 degrees?
82389.e: When it is colder than 0 degrees, we call it frost. Then water freezes outdoors.
82389.m: When there is frost, it is colder than zero degrees.

82390.q: Which three states can water have?
82390.e: Water can be solid as ice, liquid as water and a gas as steam. These are called states of matter.
82390.m: Water can be solid, liquid or gas.

82391.q: What state is an ice cube in?
82391.e: An ice cube is hard and keeps its shape. That is why it is solid.

82392.q: What state is water vapour in?
82392.e: Water vapour is a gas. It spreads out in the air and is invisible.
82392.m: Water vapour is water as a gas.

82393.q: What do you call it when ice turns into water?
82393.e: When ice gets warm, it becomes liquid. This process is called melting.
82393.m: When ice melts, it turns into water.

82394.q: What do you call it when a liquid becomes solid, for example hot wax?
82394.e: When a liquid cools, at some point it becomes solid. This process is called solidifying.
82394.m: When solidifying, a liquid becomes solid.

82395.q: What state is the lava that flows out of a volcano in?
82395.e: Lava is rock so hot that it flows. When it cools, it turns back into solid rock.

82396.q: What do you call it when water turns into steam while boiling?
82396.e: When boiling, liquid water quickly changes into a gas. This is called vaporising.
82396.m: When vaporising, a liquid turns into a gas.

82397.q: What shape are snowflakes when you look at them under a magnifying glass?
82397.e: Snowflakes are small ice crystals. They almost always have six arms or points.

82398.q: What happens to a blown-up balloon if you put it in the fridge?
82398.e: Cold air takes up less space than warm air. That is why the balloon shrinks a little.

82399.q: What can happen to a fully blown-up balloon in the hot sun?
82399.e: Warm air takes up more space. If the balloon is already full, the skin can tear.

82400.q: Why does an open balloon whizz around the room when you let go of it?
a: The air rushing out pushes it
It is pulled by the lamp
A gust of wind carries it
82400.e: The air rushes out of the back of the balloon. As it does, it pushes the balloon in the opposite direction. This is called recoil.
82400.m: Air rushing out drives a balloon forward.

82401.q: What are most balloons made of?
82401.e: Most balloons are made of rubber, or more exactly natural rubber. Rubber can stretch a lot.
82401.m: Balloons are made of stretchy rubber.

82402.q: Why does a balloon stick to the wall after you have rubbed it on your hair?
82402.e: When rubbed, the balloon gets an electric charge. This holds it to the wall.
82402.m: Rubbing gives a balloon an electric charge.

82403.q: Why does a helium balloon go limp after a few days?
a: The gas slowly escapes through the skin
82403.e: Helium particles are tiny. Little by little they slip out through the balloon skin.
82403.m: A helium balloon slowly loses its gas.

82404.q: Why does a balloon go bang when you prick it with a needle?
a: The air inside escapes all at once
82404.e: The air in the balloon is squashed together. When the skin tears, the air shoots out suddenly, and that makes the bang.
82404.m: A balloon goes bang because the air escapes suddenly.

82405.q: What happens if you blow up a balloon far too much?
82405.e: Rubber can only stretch up to a limit. If the skin gets too thin, it tears.
82405.m: A balloon blown up too much bursts.

82406.q: Why should you not leave bits of balloon lying around in nature?
82406.e: Birds, cows or wild animals sometimes mistake bits of balloon for food. This can make them ill.
82406.m: Bits of balloon belong in the bin.

82407.q: Which organ do we breathe with?
82407.e: Air goes through the nose or mouth into the lungs. There the oxygen passes into the blood.

82408.q: What do green plants give off into the air that we need to breathe?
82408.e: With the help of sunlight, plants make food from air and water. As they do, they give off oxygen, which we breathe in.
82408.m: Plants give off oxygen into the air.

82409.q: Why is the air we breathe out moist?
82409.e: In the lungs the air picks up moisture. That is why breathed-out air contains a lot of water vapour.

82410.q: Why should a classroom be aired regularly?
a: So that stale air gets out
So that the room gets darker
So that the floor gets clean
So that the lights shine brighter
82410.e: Lots of people in a room breathe out a lot of carbon dioxide. Airing lets fresh air in, and you can concentrate better.

82411.q: Through which part of the body is it best to breathe in, because it warms and cleans the air?
82411.e: In the nose the air is warmed and moistened. Tiny hairs hold back dust.
82411.m: The nose warms and cleans the air we breathe.

82412.q: What do divers need to be able to breathe underwater?
82412.e: A compressed air tank holds a lot of squashed-together air. The diver can breathe from it through a hose.
82412.m: Divers take their air with them in a tank.

82413.q: Which animal breathes underwater with gills?
82413.e: Fish take oxygen out of the water with their gills. Dolphins and whales, on the other hand, breathe air at the surface with lungs.

82414.q: What is the tube called through which the air we breathe goes from the throat to the lungs?
82414.e: The windpipe leads from the throat down to the lungs. The gullet next to it takes food to the stomach.
82414.m: The air we breathe flows through the windpipe.

82415.q: Which gas makes the bubbles in fizzy mineral water?
82415.e: Carbon dioxide is pressed into mineral water, or it is already in the spring water. In water it is often called carbonic acid.
82415.m: The bubbles in mineral water are carbon dioxide.

82416.q: What happens when you open a fizzy drink bottle that has been shaken?
82416.e: Shaking forms lots of gas bubbles. When you open the bottle, they escape all at once and carry water with them.
82416.m: Shaken fizzy bottles spray when opened.

82417.q: Why does mineral water taste flat if the bottle has been left open for a long time?
82417.e: The carbon dioxide gradually escapes into the air as a gas. Then the water no longer tingles.
82417.m: Open fizzy water loses its bubbles.

82418.q: Which of these drinks normally has no fizz?
82418.e: Cola, lemonade and sparkling water contain carbon dioxide. Milk does not fizz.

82419.q: Where does the fizz stay in the water longer?
82419.e: Cold water can hold more gas than warm. That is why a cool mineral water stays fizzy longer.
82419.m: Cold fizzy water stays bubbly longer.

82420.q: What do you hear when you open a fizzy drink bottle?
82420.e: In the closed bottle the gas is under pressure. When you open it, some of it rushes out with a hiss.
82420.m: A fizzy bottle hisses when opened.

82421.q: Is there spring water that is naturally fizzy?
82421.e: Some water takes up carbon dioxide deep underground. In Switzerland there are such springs, for example, in the Lower Engadine near Scuol.
82421.m: Some mineral springs are naturally fizzy.

82422.q: What is a device called that makes tap water fizzy at home?
82422.e: A sparkling water maker presses carbon dioxide from a gas canister into the water. This makes bubbles.
82422.m: With a sparkling water maker you can make fizzy water yourself.

82423.q: What does fizzy mineral water feel like in your mouth?
82423.e: The little gas bubbles burst on your tongue. You feel this as a tingle.

82424.q: What can a paper coffee filter take out of dirty water?
82424.e: Grains of sand are too big for the tiny holes in the paper. They get caught in the filter.
82424.m: A paper filter holds back sand.

82425.q: Can a paper filter take the salt out of salt water?
82425.e: Dissolved salt has broken up into tiny particles. These fit through every hole in the paper.
82425.m: Dissolved substances cannot simply be filtered out.

82426.q: Which layers are often used for a home-made water filter?
82426.e: The coarse gravel holds back big pieces, the sand smaller ones. The cotton wool catches the fine bits left over.
82426.m: Gravel, sand and cotton wool make cloudy water clearer.

82427.q: Which kind of carbon is found in many water filters?
82427.e: Activated carbon has a huge number of tiny pores. Smells and tastes get stuck to them.

82428.q: How is rainwater cleaned in nature before it becomes groundwater?
a: It seeps through gravel and sand
82428.e: On its way through soil, sand and gravel, a lot of dirt gets caught. The ground acts like a big filter.

82429.q: What is a plant called that turns lake water into drinking water?
82429.e: In a lake water works, water from the lake is filtered and cleaned. Zurich and Geneva, for example, get part of their drinking water this way.
82429.m: A lake water works turns lake water into drinking water.

82430.q: What does a tea strainer hold back?
82430.e: The hot water flows through the tiny holes. The tea leaves stay in the strainer.
82430.m: A tea strainer holds back the leaves.

82431.q: Why does a simple sand filter not make stream water safe to drink?
a: The sand makes the water salty
The water disappears into the sand
82431.e: A simple filter makes the water clearer. But it cannot reliably hold back very small germs.
82431.m: Clear water is not always clean drinking water.

82432.q: Which of these objects floats on water?
82432.e: Cork is very light and full of tiny air pockets. That is why a cork floats on top.
82432.m: A cork always floats on top.

82433.q: Why can a big steel ship float?
a: It is full of air inside
82433.e: A lump of steel would sink. But a ship is hollow and pushes aside a lot of water, so the water carries it.

82434.q: What helps small children stay up when learning to swim?
82434.e: Armbands are filled with air. They hold up the arms and so keep the child at the surface.

82435.q: What is the force with which water pushes things upwards called?
82435.e: Water pushes from below against everything in it. This force is called buoyancy.
82435.m: Buoyancy pushes things in water upwards.

82436.q: What happens if you shape a sinking ball of modelling clay into a flat little boat?
82436.e: As a boat, the clay pushes aside much more water. So the buoyancy is enough to carry it.
82436.m: Shape helps decide whether something floats.

82437.q: Why can you lie on the surface of the Dead Sea almost without moving?
82437.e: The Dead Sea contains much more salt than other seas. This water holds up the body especially well.
82437.m: In the Dead Sea you float like a cork.

82438.q: Which animals often have a swim bladder to hover in the water?
82438.e: Many fish have a gas-filled swim bladder in their belly. With it they hover in the water without sinking.
82438.m: The swim bladder helps fish hover.

82439.q: What does an apple do when you put it in a bucket of water?
82439.e: An apple contains a lot of air between its cells. That is why it floats on top.

82440.q: Why do children wear a life jacket on a boat?
a: It keeps their head above water
It protects them from the sun
82440.e: If you fall into the water, the life jacket holds you up. This keeps your head above the surface.
82440.m: A life jacket keeps you above water.

82441.q: What do you call a mixture in which a substance is completely dissolved in water?
82441.e: When sugar or salt has completely disappeared into water, a clear solution forms. You can no longer see any grains in it.
82441.m: A dissolved substance and water make a solution.

82442.q: Why can't you see dissolved sugar in water any more?
a: It has broken up into tiny particles
It has flown into the air
82442.e: The sugar is still there, but it has broken up into particles so small that you cannot see them.
82442.m: Dissolved sugar is invisible, but still there.

82443.q: What happens when you pour squash into water and stir?
82443.e: When stirred, squash spreads evenly through the water. The whole drink becomes sweet and coloured.

82444.q: What does water with a lot of salt dissolved in it look like?
82444.e: Dissolved salt particles are so small that light gets through. The salt water looks like normal water.
82444.m: Salt water looks like pure water.

82445.q: What is the liquid called in which a substance dissolves, for example water in sugar water?
82445.e: The water dissolves the sugar. That is why it is called a solvent.
82445.m: Water is the most important solvent.

82446.q: What happens to a sugar cube in cold water if you don't stir?
82446.e: The sugar dissolves even without stirring. But it takes much longer.
82446.m: Sugar dissolves even without stirring, just more slowly.

82447.q: Does a glass of water get heavier if you dissolve salt in it?
a: Yes, the salt is still in it
82447.e: The salt has only broken up into tiny particles. It is still in the water and weighs just as much as before.

a: Water with dissolved substances from leaves
82448.e: In hot water, colour, scent and flavour dissolve out of the leaves. The leaves themselves are left behind.
82448.m: Tea contains dissolved substances from leaves.

82449.q: Can you drink water from the tap in Switzerland?
82449.e: Tap water in Switzerland is strictly checked. You can drink it without worrying.
82449.m: Swiss tap water is good drinking water.

82450.q: What does the sign ‘Not drinking water’ on a fountain mean?
a: You should not drink the water
82450.e: At some fountains the water is not checked as drinking water. The sign warns you not to drink it.
82450.m: If it says ‘Not drinking water’, don't drink from the fountain.

82451.q: Why can't you simply drink seawater?
82451.e: Seawater contains a great deal of salt. If you drink it, you get even thirstier.
82451.m: Seawater is too salty to drink.

82452.q: Which Swiss city is known for over 1200 public fountains?
82452.e: The city of Zurich has over 1200 fountains. Fresh drinking water flows from most of them.
82452.m: Zurich is a city of fountains.

82453.q: Which drink is the best thirst quencher?
82453.e: Water quenches your thirst and has no sugar. Sweet drinks should only be drunk now and then.
82453.m: Water is the best thirst quencher.

82454.q: What is the water that comes out of the tap at home called?
82454.e: The water flows through pipes all the way to your home and out of the tap. That is why it is called tap water.
82454.m: Tap water comes out of the tap.

82455.q: What is the large store in which drinking water for a village is collected called?
82455.e: In the reservoir, clean drinking water is stored, often on a hill. From there it flows under pressure into the houses.

82456.q: What does it mean when people say the drinking water is ‘hard’?
a: It contains a lot of lime
82456.e: Hard water contains a lot of dissolved lime from the ground. You can see this from white marks in the basin or the kettle.
82456.m: Hard water contains a lot of lime.

83330.q: What is a candle usually made of?
83330.e: Candles are usually made of wax. The wax is the candle's fuel.
83330.m: A candle is usually made of wax.

83331.q: What material is a candle's wick usually made of?
83331.e: The wick is usually made of plaited cotton threads. They soak up the liquid wax well.
83331.m: A candle wick is usually made of cotton.

83332.q: What happens to the wax close to a candle's flame?
83332.e: The heat of the flame melts the wax. The liquid wax rises up the wick and burns there.
83332.m: The heat of the flame makes the wax liquid.

83333.q: Which animals provide wax for candles?
83333.e: Bees build their honeycombs from wax. Candles can be made from this beeswax.

83334.q: Why should you never put a candle right next to a curtain?
83334.e: Fabric burns easily. If the curtain moves towards the flame, a fire can start.
83334.m: Candles need to be kept away from anything that can burn.

83335.q: What do you do with a burning candle before leaving the room?
a: You put it by the window
83335.e: A candle must never burn without someone watching. Anyone who goes out blows it out first.
83335.m: Never leave a burning candle alone.

83336.q: What is the best thing to stand a candle on?
83336.e: A sturdy candle holder does not burn and does not tip over so easily. Cushions, paper and blankets can catch fire.
83336.m: A candle belongs on a sturdy holder that does not burn.

83337.q: What colour is the bottom part of a candle flame?
83337.e: Right at the bottom, the flame gets a lot of air and burns bluish. Further up it glows yellow.
83337.m: At the bottom, a candle flame is blue.

83338.q: Which way does a candle flame point?
83338.e: Hot air is lighter than cold air and rises. That is why the flame points upwards.
83338.m: A flame points upwards because hot air rises.

83340.q: Which gas from the air does a flame need?
83340.e: Fire needs oxygen to burn. Oxygen is part of the air.
83340.m: A flame needs oxygen from the air.

83341.q: What is the picture of the three things a fire needs called?
83341.e: Fire needs something that burns, air and enough heat. If one of them is missing, the fire goes out.
83341.m: The fire triangle shows what a fire needs to burn.

83342.q: What is a tiny glowing bit that jumps out of a fire called?
83342.e: Glowing bits can fly out of a fire. Sparks like these can set other things alight.
83342.m: A spark is a tiny glowing bit.

83343.q: What do you call a big fire that has got out of control?
83343.e: A blaze is a fire that spreads when nobody wants it to. It can destroy houses and forests.
83343.m: A fire out of control is called a blaze.

83344.q: What usually happens if you blow hard on a candle flame?
83344.e: The puff of air blows the hot gases away and cools the flame. Then it goes out.
83344.m: Blowing hard puts out a candle flame.

83345.e: A campfire is made outside at a safe fireplace. You can sit by it and roast sausages.
83345.m: A campfire burns outdoors at a fireplace.

83347.q: What is the stick of a match usually made of?
83347.e: The stick is a thin piece of wood. It burns once the head has caught fire.
83347.m: A match usually has a wooden stick.

83348.q: What is the thick part at the end of a match called?
83348.e: At the end is the match head. It contains substances that catch fire when rubbed.
83348.m: The head of a match catches fire when rubbed.

83349.q: Where does a safety match light?
a: On the striking surface of the box
83349.e: Safety matches only light when you strike them on the striking surface of the box. That is why they are called safety matches.
83349.m: A safety match lights on the striking surface of the box.

83350.q: Which substance is in the striking surface of a matchbox?
83350.e: The striking surface contains red phosphorus. Striking produces so much heat that the match head catches fire.
83350.m: The striking surface contains red phosphorus.

83351.q: In which country was the safety match invented?
83351.e: The safety match was invented in Sweden around 1844. That is why they are sometimes called Swedish matches.
83351.m: The safety match comes from Sweden.

83352.q: When may small children use matches?
83352.e: Accidents happen quickly with fire. That is why children only practise lighting matches together with adults.
83352.m: Children only light matches with adults.

83353.q: Apart from a match, what can you use to light a candle?
83353.e: A lighter makes a small flame. A torch only makes light, not fire.
83353.m: A lighter can also light a candle.

83354.q: What do you often smell first when something is burning somewhere?
83354.e: When something burns, it makes smoke with a sharp smell. You often smell it before you see the fire.
83354.m: A burning smell can be the first sign of a fire.

83355.q: Why should you crawl along the floor in a smoke-filled room?
a: There is less smoke down low
83355.e: In a fire, the air near the floor stays clean for longer. There you can breathe and see better.
83355.m: In smoke, crawl along the floor because the air is better there.

83356.q: What is often the most dangerous thing in a fire in a flat?
83356.e: Smoke is poisonous and spreads very fast. Just a few breaths can make you pass out.
83356.m: Smoke from a fire is very dangerous because it is poisonous.

83357.e: Smoke contains hot gases and very fine particles. The particles make the smoke visible.
83357.m: Smoke is made of gases and tiny particles.

83358.q: What does smoke coming from a chimney on the roof show?
a: A fire is burning in the stove
It is raining in the house
83358.e: When wood burns in the stove, the smoke goes out through the chimney. That is why you see it on the roof.
83358.m: Smoke from the chimney shows that a fire is burning in the stove.

83359.q: What does smoke often do to your eyes?
83359.e: The particles and gases in smoke irritate the eyes. That is why they sting and water.

83360.q: Complete the saying: ‘There's no smoke without ...’
83360.e: Smoke almost always comes from a fire. The saying means that every rumour has a reason behind it.
83360.m: Where there is smoke, there is usually fire.

83361.q: What do you do if there is smoke in the stairwell while you are in the flat?
a: Keep the door shut and call for help
83361.e: You can suffocate in a smoke-filled stairwell. The closed door keeps the smoke out until the fire brigade arrives.
83361.m: If there is smoke in the stairwell, stay behind the closed door.

83362.q: What rises above a sooty candle?
a: A thin black thread of smoke
83362.e: If a candle burns unsteadily, for example because the wick is too long, soot rises as a dark thread. Then you trim the wick.
83362.m: A sooty candle often has a wick that is too long.

83363.q: What is soot mainly made of?
83363.e: Soot is mainly made of tiny particles of carbon. They are left over when something does not burn completely.

83364.q: When is a lot of soot produced?
a: When something burns with too little air
83364.e: If there is not enough air, the fuel does not burn completely. Then black particles are left over.
83364.m: Too little air produces a lot of soot.

83365.q: Why does a candle flame glow yellow?
83365.e: Tiny soot particles form in the flame. They get very hot and glow yellow.
83365.m: Glowing soot particles make the candle flame yellow.

83366.q: What appears if you hold a cold spoon in a candle flame for a moment?
83366.e: The flame cools down on the cold spoon. The soot settles as a black spot.
83366.m: A cold spoon in the flame turns black from soot.

83367.q: Who cleans the soot out of chimneys?
83367.e: The chimney sweep cleans chimneys and stoves. That way the soot cannot catch fire and the smoke can escape properly.
83367.m: The chimney sweep cleans the soot out of the chimney.

83368.q: Which job is thought to bring good luck?
83368.e: In the past, the chimney sweep protected houses from fires. That is why chimney sweeps are still thought to bring good luck today.
83368.m: The chimney sweep is thought to bring good luck.

83369.q: What was black ink for writing made from in the past?
83369.e: Soot was mixed with water and glue. This made black ink for writing and painting.
83369.m: Black ink used to be made from soot.

83370.q: Where does wood ash go once it has cooled down completely?
83370.e: Completely cold ash with no embers may go in the rubbish. It does not belong in the recycling collections.
83370.m: Cooled ash belongs in the rubbish.

83371.q: What colour is wood ash usually?
83371.e: Wood ash is usually light grey to grey. It is a soft powder.

83372.q: Why should ash not be emptied into the rubbish bag straight away?
a: There may still be embers in it
83372.e: Embers can stay hidden in ash for a long time. In the rubbish bag they could start a fire.
83372.m: Embers can stay hidden in ash for a long time.

83373.q: What is the safest thing to keep fresh ash in?
a: A metal bucket with a lid
83373.e: Metal does not burn. The lid keeps air away, so leftover embers cannot set anything alight.
83373.m: Fresh ash goes in a metal bucket with a lid.

83374.q: How heavy is the ash compared with the wood before?
83374.e: When it burns, almost all of the wood turns into gases. Only a small amount is left behind as ash.
83374.m: Ash is much lighter than the wood was.

83375.q: What did people make from wood ash and fat in the past?
83375.e: An alkali was made from wood ash and water. Boiled with fat, it turned into soap.
83375.m: In the past, soap was made from ash and fat.

83376.q: What do some gardeners use wood ash for?
83376.e: Wood ash contains substances that plants need. That is why some people sprinkle small amounts of it in the garden.
83376.m: Wood ash can be a fertiliser for plants.

83377.q: What are the still glowing remains of a fire called?
83377.e: Embers glow red and are very hot, even without a flame. Never touch them.
83377.m: Embers are the glowing remains of a fire.

83378.q: What colour are fire extinguishers usually?
83378.e: Fire extinguishers are usually red. That way you can find them quickly in an emergency.

83379.q: What is a fire extinguisher for?
83379.e: With a fire extinguisher you can fight a small fire. Big fires are put out by the fire brigade.
83379.m: A fire extinguisher puts out small fires.

83380.q: What pushes the extinguishing agent out of a fire extinguisher?
83380.e: Inside the fire extinguisher is a gas under pressure. When you squeeze the handle, it forces the extinguishing agent through the hose.
83380.m: A gas under pressure drives the agent out of the fire extinguisher.

83381.q: What comes out of a foam extinguisher?
83381.e: A foam extinguisher sprays foam. The foam covers what is burning and cools it.
83381.m: A foam extinguisher puts out fires with foam.

83382.q: What do you have to pull out before a fire extinguisher will work?
83382.e: A pin locks the handle. Only when it has been pulled out can you put out the fire.
83382.m: With a fire extinguisher, you first pull out the safety pin.

83383.q: Where do you aim the jet of a fire extinguisher?
a: At the base of the burning object
Into the air above the fire
83383.e: You put out the fire where it is really burning, at the bottom where it starts. Spraying into the smoke does little good.
83383.m: Aim at the bottom of the burning object, not into the smoke.

83384.q: Where is a fire extinguisher usually kept in a school building?
a: On the wall where it is easy to see
83384.e: In an emergency you have to find the fire extinguisher quickly. That is why it hangs where it is easy to see in the corridor, often with a sign.
83384.m: Fire extinguishers hang on the wall where they are easy to see.

83385.q: Who should use a fire extinguisher?
83385.e: A fire extinguisher is heavy and must be used properly. Children fetch help and get themselves to safety.
83385.m: Fire extinguishers are used by adults.

83386.q: About how long can a small fire extinguisher spray for?
83386.e: A small hand-held fire extinguisher is often empty after only about 10 to 20 seconds. That is why you have to aim carefully.
83386.m: A small fire extinguisher is empty after just a few seconds.

83387.q: What is a fire blanket for?
83387.e: You cover a small fire with a fire blanket. This smothers it.
83387.m: A fire blanket smothers small fires.

83388.q: How does a fire blanket put out a fire?
a: It takes the air away from the fire
83388.e: Under the blanket no fresh air can reach the fire. Without air it goes out.
83388.m: The fire blanket takes away the fire's air.

83389.q: In which room is a fire blanket often kept?
83389.e: The kitchen is where cooking and frying happen. Oil in a pan can easily catch fire there.
83389.m: A fire blanket often hangs in the kitchen.

83390.q: What can you cover a burning pan with if there is no fire blanket?
83390.e: A metal lid does not burn and closes the pan tightly. Without air, the fire goes out.
83390.m: A lid that fits can put out a burning pan.

83391.q: What is a fire blanket often made of?
83391.e: Fire blankets are made of a fabric that does not burn, often glass fibre. Paper, plastic and silk would catch fire.
83391.m: A fire blanket is made of a fabric that does not burn.

83392.q: How do you get a fire blanket out of its case quickly?
83392.e: Two tapes hang from the case. If you pull them hard, the blanket falls out.
83392.m: Pull the tapes to get the fire blanket out.

83393.q: Why do you hold the fire blanket so that your hands are behind it?
83393.e: The blanket is like a shield in front of the flames. That way you don't burn your hands.
83393.m: Behind the fire blanket, your hands are protected.

83394.q: What do you do with the fire blanket after covering the pan?
a: You pull it off at once
83394.e: It can stay hot under the blanket for a long time. If you lift it off too soon, the fire can flare up again.
83394.m: Leave the fire blanket in place until everything has cooled down.

83395.q: What does a smoke alarm do when it detects smoke?
83395.e: A smoke alarm makes a very loud warning sound. That way everyone is warned, even while asleep.
83395.m: A smoke alarm warns with a loud beep.

83396.q: Where is a smoke alarm fitted?
83396.e: The smoke alarm detects smoke where it gathers first in a room. That way it warns as early as possible.
83396.m: A smoke alarm belongs on the ceiling.

83397.q: What does a smoke alarm usually need in order to work?
83397.e: Most smoke alarms have a battery. That way they work even in a power cut.
83397.m: A smoke alarm usually needs a battery.

83398.q: How do you check whether a smoke alarm works?
83398.e: Every smoke alarm has a test button. When you press it, the warning sound must go off.
83398.m: You check a smoke alarm with the test button.

83399.q: Why is a smoke alarm in the bedroom especially important?
a: You can't smell smoke while asleep
Cooking is done in the bedroom
83399.e: Sleeping people do not notice smoke and do not wake up from it. The loud sound of the smoke alarm wakes them.
83399.m: A smoke alarm wakes us because we can't smell smoke while asleep.

83400.q: What do you do if the smoke alarm goes off and there is a fire?
83400.e: Smoke spreads very fast. That is why you go out at once and get help outside.
83400.m: When the smoke alarm goes off, leave the flat at once.

83401.q: What does a short beep from a smoke alarm every few minutes often mean?
a: There is a fire in the cellar
83401.e: Many smoke alarms give a short beep when the battery gets weak. Then it needs changing soon.
83401.m: A short beep often means a weak battery.

83402.q: How often should you check a smoke alarm?
a: Only when there is a fire
83402.e: Only a working smoke alarm can warn you. That is why you check it regularly with the test button.

83403.q: What shape are the hazard symbols on chemicals?
83403.e: The hazard symbols are diamonds, that is squares standing on one corner. Inside is a black picture.

83404.q: What colour is the border of a hazard symbol?
83404.e: Hazard symbols have a red border and a white background. The black picture shows the danger.
83404.m: Hazard symbols have a red border.

83405.q: What does the hazard symbol with a flame mean?
83405.e: The flame shows that this substance can catch fire easily. Keep it away from heat and flames.
83405.m: The flame symbol warns of highly flammable substances.

83406.q: What does the hazard symbol with a skull and crossbones mean?
83406.e: The skull and crossbones warns of very poisonous substances. Even small amounts can be deadly.
83406.m: The skull and crossbones warns of poison.

83407.q: What does the hazard symbol with a dead tree and a fish mean?
83407.e: This substance harms animals and plants, especially in water. It must not go down the drain.
83407.m: The tree and fish warn of danger to the environment.

83408.q: What does the hazard symbol with an exploding bomb mean?
83408.e: The exploding bomb warns of substances that can explode. You have to be very careful with them.
83408.m: The bomb warns of explosive substances.

83409.q: What does the hazard symbol with a flame over a circle mean?
83409.e: Such substances give off oxygen. They make a fire stronger, even if they do not burn themselves.
83409.m: The flame over a circle warns of oxidising substances.

83410.q: On which things at home do you often find hazard symbols?
83410.e: Many cleaning products contain dangerous substances. That is why they carry hazard symbols.
83410.m: Many cleaning products carry hazard symbols.

83411.q: What does the hazard symbol with drops attacking a hand mean?
83411.e: Corrosive substances can injure skin and eyes. That is why the symbol shows a hand being attacked.
83411.m: The symbol with the hand warns of corrosive substances.

83412.q: What is the first thing you do in a fire?
83412.e: The rule is: raise the alarm, rescue, put out. First you call for help, then you get people to safety.
83412.m: In a fire, first raise the alarm, then rescue, then put it out.

83413.q: What should you do if your own clothes are on fire?
83413.e: Running gives the fire more air. If you lie down and roll, you smother the flames.
83413.m: If your clothes are on fire, lie down and roll.

83414.q: What do you use to get out of a building on fire?
83414.e: The lift can get stuck in a fire. That is why you always take the stairs.
83414.m: In a fire, take the stairs, never the lift.

83415.q: Why do you close the door when leaving a room on fire?
a: It holds back smoke and fire
83415.e: A closed door slows down smoke and flames. That way the escape route stays clear for longer.
83415.m: A closed door slows down smoke and fire.

83416.q: What colour are emergency exit signs?
83416.e: Emergency exits and escape routes are marked with green signs. They show a white figure running to a door.

83417.q: What should you not do when escaping from a fire?
83417.e: Looking for things wastes precious time. People are more important than things.
83417.m: In a fire, save yourself, not your toys.

83418.q: Where does everyone meet during a fire drill at school?
83418.e: After leaving the school building, everyone goes to the assembly point. There the teacher can see whether everyone is there.
83418.m: After a fire alarm, everyone meets at the assembly point.

83419.q: Who comes in red vehicles to put out fires?
83419.e: The fire brigade drives red vehicles with blue lights. It puts out fires and rescues people.
83419.m: The fire brigade puts out fires and rescues people.

83420.q: What is barbecue charcoal made from?
83420.e: Barbecue charcoal is charcoal made from wood. Wood is heated with little air until it turns into charcoal.
83420.m: Barbecue charcoal is made from wood.

83421.q: What is the job of people who make charcoal called?
83421.e: Charcoal burners turn wood into charcoal in a big pile. In the Entlebuch in the canton of Lucerne there are still charcoal burners today.

83422.q: What is the big pile of wood in which charcoal burners make charcoal called?
83422.e: In a charcoal kiln, wood is covered with earth. It smoulders there for days with little air and turns into charcoal.
83422.m: In a charcoal kiln, wood turns into charcoal.

83423.q: What must you never pour onto glowing barbecue charcoal?
83423.e: Methylated spirits and petrol evaporate and catch fire explosively. A dangerous jet of flame shoots up.
83423.m: Never pour methylated spirits or petrol onto glowing charcoal.

83424.q: How can you tell that the barbecue charcoal is ready for grilling?
a: It is covered in grey ash
83424.e: When the charcoal is glowing right through, a grey layer lies on it. Then it gives off even heat.
83424.m: Grey charcoal is ready for grilling.

83425.q: Why must you never use a charcoal barbecue in a closed room?
a: The charcoal goes out at once
83425.e: Glowing charcoal produces carbon monoxide. This gas is poisonous and you cannot smell it.
83425.m: A charcoal barbecue belongs outdoors only.

83426.q: What do you use to light barbecue charcoal safely?
83426.e: Firelighters burn slowly and evenly. That way the charcoal lights without a jet of flame.

83427.q: What do you use to turn sausages on a hot barbecue?
83427.e: Barbecue tongs are long and made of metal. That way your fingers stay well away from the embers.

84312.q: Which metal is steel mainly made from?
84312.e: Steel is iron with a little carbon. This makes it stronger and tougher.
84312.m: Steel is mainly made of iron.

84313.q: Which metal does our blood need to carry oxygen?
84313.e: The red pigment in blood contains iron. It binds oxygen and carries it all round the body.
84313.m: The red pigment in blood contains iron.

84314.q: Where does the iron that nails are made from come from?
84314.e: Iron is found in certain rocks called iron ore. They are dug out of the ground and the iron is melted out.
84314.m: Iron comes from rocks in the ground.

84315.q: Where is iron ore melted into iron?
84315.e: A blast furnace is a huge furnace that gets very hot. Inside it, the ore turns into liquid iron.
84315.m: In a blast furnace, iron ore becomes iron.

84316.q: What happens to iron if it lies outside in the rain for a long time?
84316.e: Water and air attack the iron. Brown rust forms.

84317.q: Which famous tower in Paris is built of iron?
84317.e: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 from many thousands of iron parts. They are held together with rivets.
84317.m: The Eiffel Tower in Paris is made of iron.

84318.q: What happens to an iron nail that you put in water?
84318.e: Iron is much heavier than the same amount of water. That is why an iron nail sinks at once.
84318.m: An iron nail sinks in water.

84319.q: What happens if you stroke an iron nail many times in the same direction with a magnet?
84319.e: Stroking turns the nail itself into a weak magnet. Then it can pick up small paper clips.
84319.m: An iron nail can become a magnet itself.

84320.q: What are heavy, dark frying pans often made of?
84320.e: Cast iron is iron that is poured into a mould while liquid. Such pans are heavy and hold the heat for a long time.
84320.m: Heavy frying pans are often made of cast iron.

84321.q: What colour is freshly polished copper?
84321.e: Copper is one of the few metals with a colour of its own. It shines reddish brown.

84323.q: Which reddish metal are some expensive cooking pots made of?
84323.e: Copper pots shine reddish. Cooks like them because they heat up quickly and evenly.
84323.m: Some cooking pots are made of copper.

84324.q: Why are some pan bases made of copper?
84324.e: Copper passes on the heat from the hob quickly. This makes the whole pan evenly hot.

84325.q: Which metal is the outer skin of the Statue of Liberty in New York made of?
84325.e: The Statue of Liberty has a skin of thin copper sheets. It used to shine reddish brown, but today it is green.
84325.m: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper on the outside.

84326.q: What is the period called when people first made tools from copper?
84326.e: Copper was one of the first metals people used. The Copper Age lies at the end of the New Stone Age.
84326.m: In the Copper Age, people made their first tools from copper.

84327.q: What can you easily do with a thin copper wire?
84327.e: Copper is soft and bends well. That is why you can shape figures from copper wire.

84328.q: What is copper wire very often used for in the home?
84328.e: Electric cables contain copper wires. Copper conducts electricity very well.

84329.q: What does pure, polished silver look like?
84329.e: Silver is a bright, white, shiny metal. It reflects light very well.

84330.q: What happens to silver cutlery that lies in the drawer for a long time?
84330.e: Silver reacts with traces of sulphur in the air. This forms a dark layer; we say it tarnishes.
84330.m: Silver tarnishes and goes dark over time.

84331.q: How does tarnished silver become shiny again?
84331.e: When polishing, you rub away the dark layer. Afterwards the silver shines brightly again.
84331.m: Polishing makes tarnished silver beautiful again.

84332.q: Which place gets a silver medal at the Olympic Games?
84332.e: The silver medal is for second place. The winner gets the gold medal.

84333.q: Which metal is more expensive than silver?
84333.e: Gold is much rarer than silver. That is why it costs a great deal more per gram.
84333.m: Gold is more valuable than silver.

84334.q: Which metal conducts electricity best of all?
84334.e: Silver conducts electricity even better than copper. But because it is expensive, copper is usually used for cables.
84334.m: Silver conducts electricity best of all metals.

84335.q: What is the wedding anniversary after 25 years of marriage called?
84335.e: After 25 years of marriage, people celebrate their silver wedding. After 50 years it is the golden wedding.
84335.m: After 25 years, people celebrate their silver wedding.

84336.q: What is silver especially often used for?
84336.e: Silver shines beautifully and does not rust. That is why rings, necklaces and earrings are often made from it.
84336.m: Jewellery is often made from silver.

84337.q: Which of these metals is especially light?
84337.e: Aluminium weighs only about a third as much as the same amount of iron. That is why it is called a light metal.

84338.q: What are many drinks cans made of?
84338.e: Drinks cans are usually made of thin aluminium. They are light and protect the drink well.
84338.m: Many drinks cans are made of aluminium.

84339.q: Which rock is aluminium obtained from?
84339.e: Bauxite is a reddish rock with a lot of aluminium in it. Using a lot of electricity, aluminium is made from it.

84340.q: What are large parts of many aeroplanes made of?
84340.e: An aeroplane has to be strong but still light. That is why many parts are made of aluminium.
84340.m: Many aeroplane parts are made of aluminium.

84341.q: What do you save when you recycle old aluminium?
84341.e: Making new aluminium takes a great deal of electricity. Melting down old aluminium needs only a small part of that.
84341.m: Recycling aluminium saves a lot of energy.

84342.e: In air, aluminium forms a very thin protective layer. This protects the metal, so it does not rust.

84343.q: What are light bike frames often made of?
84343.e: Aluminium bike frames are strong and light. That way you can easily carry the bike.
84343.m: Light bike frames are often made of aluminium.

84344.e: Aluminium is a shiny, silvery grey metal. It looks a bit like silver but is much cheaper.

84345.q: Which small toy figures used to be cast from a soft, silvery metal?
84345.e: Tin figures are made by pouring liquid tin into moulds. Tin soldiers used to be a popular toy.
84345.m: Tin figures are cast from tin.

84346.q: Which of these metals melts at quite a low heat?
84346.e: Tin melts at only about 232 degrees. Iron and copper need well over 1000 degrees.
84346.m: Tin melts at a low heat.

84347.e: Tin is a shiny, silvery white metal. It looks a bit like silver.

84348.q: What do you use to join electric wires when soldering?
84348.e: Solder melts on the hot soldering iron and flows around the wires. As it cools, it sets and holds them together.
84348.m: When soldering, wires are joined with solder.

84349.q: What were many plates, mugs and jugs made of in the past?
84349.e: Tinware used to be found in many households. Today it is often collected as an ornament.
84349.m: In the past, people often ate from tin plates.

84350.q: Which soft metal makes a faint crackling sound when you bend a bar of it?
84350.e: When bending, the tiny crystals in the tin rub against each other. This makes a faint crackle called the ‘tin cry’.
84350.m: Tin crackles when you bend it.

84351.q: What can happen to objects made of pure tin if they are exposed to great cold for a very long time?
84351.e: In great cold, tin can slowly crumble into a grey powder. This is called tin pest.
84351.m: Tin can crumble in great cold.

84352.e: Pure tin is a soft metal. It is easy to bend and shape.

84353.q: Which place gets the bronze medal in a competition?
84353.e: In many competitions the three best get a medal. The bronze medal is for third place.

84354.q: Which period came before the Bronze Age?
84354.e: At first people made tools from stone. Only later did they learn to make bronze.
84354.m: The Stone Age came before the Bronze Age.

84355.e: New bronze shines golden brown. Over time it often becomes darker or greenish.

84356.q: What are many church bells cast from?
84356.e: Bronze bells sound especially beautiful and ring for a long time. This mixture is also called bell bronze.
84356.m: Many church bells are made of bronze.

84357.q: What are many large outdoor monuments and statues made of?
84357.e: Bronze withstands wind and weather for many hundreds of years. That is why monuments are often cast from it.
84357.m: Many monuments are cast in bronze.

84358.e: Bronze is made by mixing liquid metals together. Such a mixture is called an alloy.
84358.m: Bronze is a mixture of metals.

84359.q: Why was bronze better than pure copper for tools?
84359.e: Pure copper is quite soft. Bronze is much harder, so knives and axes stayed sharp for longer.

84360.q: What do you call pouring liquid bronze into a mould?
84360.e: The bronze is melted and poured into a mould. When it has cooled, it has taken on the shape.

84361.q: What were the villages on Swiss lake shores called where people lived in the Bronze Age?
84361.e: The houses stood on wooden stilts on the lake shore. Remains of them can still be found in many Swiss lakes today.
84361.m: In the Bronze Age, people in Switzerland lived in stilt houses.

84362.e: Rust is a reddish brown layer on iron. You can easily recognise it by its colour.

84363.q: Where does a bike rust faster?
84363.e: Iron rusts when water and air get to it. In the rain this happens much faster than in the dry.

84364.q: Which of these metals can rust?
84364.e: Rust only forms on iron and steel. Other metals change in other ways or hardly at all.

84365.q: How do you protect an iron garden gate from rust?
a: You stand it in the sun
84365.e: The paint keeps water and air away from the iron. That way the iron cannot rust so quickly.

84366.q: What happens to iron that rusts for years?
a: It becomes brittle and falls apart
84366.e: Rust eats deeper and deeper into the iron. In the end the iron gets holes and crumbles.

84367.q: Why do cars rust faster in winter?
a: Because of the snow on the roof
84367.e: In winter, salt is spread on Swiss roads. Salty water makes iron rust much faster.
84367.m: Road salt makes cars rust faster.

84368.q: What is the kitchen sink often made of, because it does not rust?
84368.e: Stainless steel is a steel that does not rust. It stays shiny even with lots of water.

84369.q: What helps to stop a bike chain from rusting?
84369.e: The oil forms a film on the chain. That way no water can reach the metal.
84369.m: Oil protects the bike chain from rust.

84370.q: Is rust still the same as iron?
a: No, it is a new substance
No, it is a kind of wood
No, it is a kind of garden soil
84370.e: When iron rusts, it combines with oxygen and water. This makes a completely new substance.

84371.q: On which metal can verdigris form?
84371.e: Verdigris is a green coating on copper. It also forms on metals that contain copper.

84372.q: What forms when copper is in contact with vinegar for a long time?
84372.e: The acid in vinegar attacks the copper. This creates a green coating called verdigris.

84373.q: Why must you never eat or lick verdigris?
84373.e: Verdigris is poisonous. That is why you should not keep food in copper pots with a green coating.

84374.q: What is the correct name for the green layer on old copper roofs?
84374.e: People often call it verdigris, but the correct name for this layer is patina. It forms slowly through air and rain.
84374.m: The green layer on copper roofs is called patina.

84375.q: Why is the green layer on a copper roof not removed?
84375.e: The green layer covers the copper like a coat. Underneath, the metal stays in good condition for many years.
84375.m: The green layer protects the copper roof.

84376.q: What did painters use verdigris for in the past?
84376.e: In the past, painters mixed a bright green paint from verdigris. Today there are non-poisonous paints for this.
84376.m: Verdigris used to be a paint.

84378.e: Brass contains copper. That is why a green coating can form on it too.
84378.m: Verdigris can also form on brass.

84379.q: What is kitchen foil used for?
84379.e: Kitchen foil can be wrapped tightly around food. That keeps it fresh or warm.
84379.m: You wrap food in kitchen foil.

84380.q: Can kitchen foil go in the microwave?
a: Yes, if it is completely smooth
Yes, if the food is cold
84380.e: Metal in the microwave can make sparks. That can damage the appliance or start a fire.
84380.m: Kitchen foil does not belong in the microwave.

84381.q: Which side of kitchen foil can you use?
84381.e: One side is dull only because of the way it is made. Both sides work almost equally well.
84381.m: You can use both sides of kitchen foil.

a: Thinner than a sheet of paper
84382.e: Kitchen foil is only about one hundredth of a millimetre thick. A sheet of paper is much thicker.
84382.m: Kitchen foil is thinner than paper.

84383.q: Why should you not wrap acidic food in kitchen foil?
84383.e: Acid from lemons or tomatoes attacks the foil. This can let aluminium get into the food.
84383.m: You do not wrap acidic food in kitchen foil.

84384.q: In which country did the first aluminium foil factory open in 1910?
84384.e: The first rolling mill for aluminium foil opened in 1910 in Kreuzlingen in the canton of Thurgau. From 1911 the foil also wrapped chocolate.
84384.m: The first aluminium foil was made in Switzerland.

84385.q: What do you do with clean, used kitchen foil in Switzerland?
a: Take it to the aluminium collection
Put it in the waste paper
Throw it in the bottle bank
84385.e: Aluminium can be melted down again and again. That is why clean foil is collected together with aluminium cans.
84385.m: Clean kitchen foil goes to the aluminium collection.

84386.q: What can you easily do with kitchen foil without any tools?
84386.e: Kitchen foil is very thin and soft. You can fold and shape it with your hands.
84386.m: Kitchen foil is easy to shape.

84387.q: What is a tin can for?
a: Keeping food for a long time
84387.e: In the sealed can, food stays good for a long time. No air and no germs can get in.
84387.m: A tin can keeps food for a long time.

84388.q: What do you use to open a tin without a ring pull?
84388.e: A tin opener cuts all the way round the lid. Then you can lift it off.
84388.m: You open tins with a tin opener.

84389.q: What is a tin can usually made of?
84389.e: Most tin cans are made of thin sheet steel. It is strong and protects the food well.
84389.m: Tin cans are usually made of sheet steel.

84390.q: Why does a tin can not rust so quickly?
a: It has a thin layer of tin
It is made of pure iron
84390.e: The sheet steel is covered with a fine layer of tin. This metal is called tinplate.
84390.m: A layer of tin protects tin cans from rust.

84391.q: What can you use to separate steel cans from aluminium cans?
84391.e: A magnet attracts steel but not aluminium. This makes the cans easy to sort.
84391.m: A magnet separates steel cans from aluminium cans.

84392.q: What does it mean if the lid of a tin bulges outwards?
a: The contents may have gone off
84392.e: When germs grow in the tin, they make gas. Then the lid bulges and you must not eat the contents.
84392.m: You throw away a bulging tin.

84393.q: What should you do with an empty tin before taking it to the collection point?
84393.e: Rinsed tins do not smell and do not attract animals. That way they can be recycled easily.
84393.m: You rinse empty tins before recycling them.

84394.q: Why is the food heated inside the sealed tin?
a: So that the tin gets lighter
84394.e: The heat kills the germs in the food. That is why the contents do not go off for so long.
84394.m: Heat kills the germs in the tin.

84395.q: How long does food usually stay good in a sealed tin?
84395.e: Tinned food often keeps for several years. The tin says until when the contents are at least good.
84395.m: Tinned food often keeps for several years.

84396.e: A smith heats metal in the fire until it glows. Then he shapes it with a hammer.

84397.q: What is a smith's workshop called?
84397.e: In the forge there is a fire, an anvil and lots of hammers. That is where the smith works.
84397.m: The smith works in the forge.

84398.q: On which heavy iron block does the smith hammer the metal?
84398.e: The anvil is a heavy block of steel. The smith lays the hot metal on it and hammers it into shape.
84398.m: The smith hammers the metal on the anvil.

84399.q: What does the smith use to hold the red-hot iron?
84399.e: The iron is far too hot to touch. With long tongs the smith holds it safely.
84399.m: The smith holds the hot iron with tongs.

84400.q: Why does the smith make the iron red-hot?
a: So it becomes soft and easy to shape
84400.e: Cold iron is hard and can hardly be shaped. Red-hot iron can be bent and stretched with a hammer.
84400.m: Red-hot iron is easy to shape.

84401.q: What is a smith who fits horseshoes on horses called?
84401.e: The farrier shapes horseshoes and fixes them to the horses' hooves. This protects the hooves.

84403.q: What does the smith use to blow air into the fire to make it hotter?
84403.e: The bellows pump air into the fire. More air makes the fire hotter.
84403.m: The smith makes the fire hotter with bellows.

84404.q: What is the smallest coin in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
84404.e: The 1-centime coin was withdrawn in 2007, and the 2-centime coin even earlier. Today the 5-centime coin is the smallest coin.
84404.m: The smallest Swiss coin is the 5-centime coin.

84405.q: What colour is the Swiss 5-centime coin?
84405.e: The 5-centime coin is made of a mixture containing copper and aluminium. That is why it shines golden yellow.

84406.q: Which female figure can be seen on Swiss 1-franc coins?
84406.e: Helvetia is a female figure who stands for Switzerland. She is shown standing with a spear and shield.

84407.q: In which city are Swiss coins made?
84407.e: The Swiss mint is called Swissmint. It is in Bern.
84407.m: Swiss coins are made in Bern.

84408.e: A machine presses the picture into a small metal disc with great force. This is called minting.

84409.q: What is the 5-franc coin often called in Switzerland?
84409.e: The 5-franc coin is the largest Swiss coin. In everyday life it is called the Fünfliber.
84409.m: The 5-franc coin is also called the Fünfliber.

84410.q: What are the two sides called when you toss a coin?
84410.e: One side shows the value, the number. The other side often shows a head or a picture.
84410.m: When you toss a coin, it is heads or tails.

84411.q: Which metals is the Swiss 1-franc coin made of?
84411.e: The shiny silver franc coins are made of copper and nickel. Until 1967 they were made of silver.
84411.m: The 1-franc coin is made of copper and nickel.

85304.e: Recyclable materials are waste such as paper, glass or metal from which something new can be made. That is why they are collected separately.
85304.m: A recyclable material is waste that still has value.

85305.q: How do you hand in waste paper in many Swiss municipalities?
a: Tied in bundles for the paper collection
85305.e: In many municipalities, people tie waste paper with string and put it out by the road on collection day. That way it can be recycled.
85305.m: Waste paper is bundled and collected separately.

85306.q: Which symbol often stands for recycling?
85306.e: The recycling symbol is made of three arrows going round in a circle. It shows that a material goes back into the cycle.
85306.m: Three arrows in a circle stand for recycling.

85307.q: Which metal are many drinks cans made of?
85307.e: Many drinks cans are made of aluminium. Old aluminium can be melted down and made into new cans.
85307.m: Aluminium drinks cans go to the aluminium collection.

85308.q: What do you call a place where you can hand in glass, cans and used oil?
85308.e: At a collection point there are containers for different recyclable materials. Everything is collected separately there.
85308.m: At the collection point you hand in recyclables separately.

85309.q: Why are recyclable materials collected separately?
85309.e: New products are made from separately collected materials. That means fewer new raw materials have to be taken from nature.
85309.m: Recycling saves raw materials from nature.

85310.q: What goes in the cardboard collection?
